entries.name: AR Video (autoregressive block sampler)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Denoises a video one block of frames at a time using a model with key-value caches, in the style of Causal Forcing and Self-Forcing. Each sub-step jumps to x0 and re-noises on the flow line with fresh noise, then a final call at σ=0 writes the block into the cache. It refuses to run on models without the cache API.

entries.name: CFG++ UD10 AB (history CFG++)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A CFG++ Euler with three additions: a small history term on the unconditional slope, a 25% blend toward a variable-step second-order Adams-Bashforth step, and a final step that extrapolates x0 down to σ=0. It can be picked by name in the sampler list, but no node exposes its parameters, which are fixed. Unlike the other CFG++ samplers it keeps the cfg=1 shortcut, and at cfg=1 it uses the cond prediction as U. The name is not explained in the code.

entries.name: DDIM (alias of Euler)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The name ddim does not have its own loop in core: the registry builds the Euler sampler with one extra inpaint option. The update is the same deterministic Euler line; only the noise used to re-noise the protected area of an inpaint mask differs. In σ coordinates Euler already has the η=0 DDIM form x'=(σ'/σ)x+(1−σ'/σ)D, so the name is not wrong, but no extra algorithm exists behind it.

entries.name: DDPM
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The classic DDPM posterior step written in VP coordinates: scale the latent into VP space, compute the mean from ε, add posterior noise, scale back. One model call per step.

entries.name: DEIS (tab mode)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A multistep exponential integrator: past slopes are weighted by coefficients integrated numerically along a VP noise schedule. In core that schedule is fixed by hard-coded EDM-to-VP constants. No node exposes its options, so sampler name means order 3, tab mode.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Second-order multistep DPM++ on x0 in −log σ: reuse the previous x0 prediction to correct the current step for one call per step. Deterministic, and the step formula has no special flow-model handling.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M CFG++
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A CFG++ rewrite of 2M: the exponential term carries the unconditional prediction while the guided x0 is added directly. The second-order correction here takes the difference between the current guided x0 and the previous unconditional x0. So unlike normal 2M it does not shrink to zero on a smooth path when guidance is on.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M SDE (Heun correction)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The same code as 2M SDE with solver_type=heun, which changes the coefficient of the second-order correction. There is no second model call despite the name: still one call per step.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M SDE (midpoint)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The 2M idea with a noise term: an exponential update on x0 in half-logSNR, a second-order correction from the previous x0, and Brownian noise. Default solver_type midpoint. η=0 removes the noise. One model call per step.

entries.name: DPM++ 2S Ancestral (flow / RF branch)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Flow-model path of dpmpp_2s_ancestral. It uses logit-based midpoint noise levels and linear interpolation toward x0, then the flow rescale and renoise. A hard-coded branch makes the first step degenerate when σ is exactly 1.

entries.name: DPM++ 2S Ancestral (VE path)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A two-stage single-step DPM++ method on x0 with ancestral noise. It evaluates at the midpoint in log σ toward σ_down and uses that second prediction for the full step. Non-flow branch; flow models use the RF entry.

entries.name: DPM++ 2S Ancestral CFG++
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A CFG++ version of 2S that shifts x by the guidance gap before each exponential step. Nothing is dispatched to RF, so flow models run the −log σ formula. Reading the code shows the second update mixes values from two different model calls.

entries.name: DPM++ 3M SDE
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Extends the multistep SDE to two previous x0 values for a third-order correction, building up from first to second order over the early steps. One model call per step, Brownian noise.

entries.name: DPM++ SDE
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A two-stage stochastic DPM++ method: noisy intermediate stage, model call, then a blended x0 for the full step with more noise. Noise comes from a Brownian tree seeded from the run seed, so each draw is a function of its σ interval. Costs two model calls per step.

entries.name: DPM-2
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A midpoint method: step to the geometric middle of σ and σ', evaluate, and use that slope for the whole step. Two model calls per step. In the KSampler path the schedule is built one step longer and the second-to-last sigma is dropped.

entries.name: DPM-2 Ancestral (flow / RF branch)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The flow-model path of dpm_2_ancestral, picked automatically. The midpoint step itself is the VE-looking formula, but it is aimed at the RF σ_down and followed by the flow-style rescale and renoise.

entries.name: DPM-2 Ancestral (VE path)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: DPM-2's midpoint step aimed at σ_down, then fresh noise added back up to σ'. Same two model calls per step as DPM-2, plus the ancestral randomness. Non-flow branch; flow models use the RF entry.

entries.name: DPM-Solver Adaptive (12/23)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An embedded pair (order 2 inside order 3, or 1 inside 2) runs with a PID step-size controller. The step count is not used at all: only the first and the last non-zero σ, and it stops there instead of jumping to zero. Rejected attempts cost model calls and the time taken varies with the error tolerance.

entries.name: DPM-Solver-Fast
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The DPM-Solver fixed-budget driver. It takes the requested step count as a model-call budget, spreads order-3 stages uniformly in log σ, and ignores the schedule apart from its end points. It stops at the last non-zero sigma instead of jumping to zero.

entries.name: ER-SDE
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Extended Reverse-Time SDE solver: first-order core with second and third stage corrections from history, using numerically integrated terms under a configurable noise scaler. The node can switch that scaler to reverse-time SDE or to plain ODE, and η controls it. One model call per step.

entries.name: Euler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The plain first-order step: ask the model for the clean image, compute the slope toward it, walk to the next noise level. With the default churn of 0 it is deterministic and costs one model call per step. It is the simplest solver in core, and several other entries reduce to this line.

entries.name: Euler Ancestral (flow / RF branch)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: What euler_ancestral silently becomes on a flow model. It interpolates toward x0 to a lower noise level, rescales the signal, and adds fresh noise so the sample sits back on the straight data-noise line. It has no name of its own: selection happens from the model type.

entries.name: Euler Ancestral (VE path)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Takes an Euler step past the next noise level, then adds fresh noise to climb back. The injected noise means the path is not a deterministic ODE path. This entry is the non-flow branch; flow models go to the RF entry.

entries.name: Euler Ancestral CFG++
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The CFG++ version of ancestral Euler: renoising follows the unconditional prediction and fresh noise is added afterward. It handles flow and non-flow models in one formula, through α factors rather than a separate RF branch. The cfg=1 shortcut is off so both passes always run.

entries.name: Euler CFG++
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An Euler step that renoises along the unconditional prediction rather than the guided one, in the CFG++ manner. It still lands on the guided x0 and is deterministic. Because it needs the unconditional output it turns off ComfyUI's cfg=1 shortcut, so cfg=1 still pays for both passes.

entries.name: Euler CFG++ (alternative, node only)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The second option of the experimental SamplerEulerCFGpp node, with no entry in the sampler list. It feeds a shifted latent into the slope helper, which produces a different formula from the regular CFG++ path. Worth knowing because its last step does not return the guided x0.

entries.name: Exponential Heun 2 (x0)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Thin preset of the SEEDS-2 code with r=1 and no noise, giving a deterministic exponential Heun method working on x0 in logSNR. The second model call is made at the next sigma rather than a midpoint. Two calls per step like Heun.

entries.name: Exponential Heun 2 (x0, SDE)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same preset with noise on (η=1). Because r=1 the intermediate stage already sits at σ', so the noise drawn for it is carried straight through to the final state. Default noise is plain seeded Gaussian, not a Brownian tree.

entries.name: Gradient Estimation
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler plus a correction from the change in slope between steps, scaled by γ=2 by default. One call per step, deterministic. With γ=2 the correction makes the step use 2d−d_old from step 2.

entries.name: Gradient Estimation CFG++
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same correction with slope taken from the unconditional prediction, and the base step using the CFG++ form. The cfg=1 shortcut is off. No α factors, so on flow models it differs from euler_cfg_pp.

entries.name: Heun
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Predicts with Euler, re-evaluates the model at the landing point, and averages the two slopes. That second call is why it costs about twice as many model calls as Euler for the same step count. Deterministic unless churn is used.

entries.name: Heun++2
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Looks two schedule entries ahead, evaluates the model at both, and blends three slopes with weights set by how far σ has fallen from the very first sigma. Weight shifts toward the first slope as σ drops, so late steps move toward Euler. Costs three model calls for most steps but moves x only one step each time.

entries.name: iPNDM
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Improved pseudo-numerical method: Adams-Bashforth history on slopes with fixed textbook coefficients, up to order 4, one call per step. The coefficients assume even step size in σ, whatever the schedule actually is. The sibling ipndm_v adapts them.

entries.name: iPNDM-v (variable step)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The variable-step version of iPNDM: same history idea, but coefficients depend on the ratios of recent step sizes in σ. Uneven steps are therefore reflected in the weights. One call per step.

entries.name: LCM
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Each step jumps directly to the model's x0 and then adds fresh noise for the next level, using the model's own noise scaling. The code states no model requirement. A node adds a noise multiplier ramp and a clamp on the injected noise.

entries.name: LCM Upscale (node only)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An LCM-style loop that enlarges the latent on a schedule between steps, so sampling and upscaling happen together. Not in the sampler list; only reached through its node. It adds noise with a raw VE formula rather than the model's noise scaling.

entries.name: LMS (linear multistep)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reuses slopes from previous steps instead of extra model calls: one call per step, up to fourth order by default. Coefficients are computed by numerically integrating Lagrange polynomials over the actual σ spacing. Deterministic.

entries.name: RES Multistep
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Second-order exponential multistep on x0, one call per step; the first step and last step are Euler. Calls the shared res_multistep function with η=0. Deterministic.

entries.name: RES Multistep Ancestral
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: RES aimed at σ_down, with fresh noise added back to σ' each step. The multistep history uses the previous σ_down rather than the σ the noise landed on. Default η=1.

entries.name: RES Multistep Ancestral CFG++
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Combines the CFG++ path and ancestral noise of res_multistep with η=1 default. cfg=1 shortcut off, no flow branch.

entries.name: RES Multistep CFG++
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: RES with the CFG++ treatment: first add the guidance gap to x, then run the exponential step on unconditional predictions. History stores U rather than D. The cfg=1 shortcut is off.

entries.name: SA-Solver
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Stochastic Adams predictor-corrector: uses a window of past x0 predictions with coefficients from exponential integrals, and noise only inside a chosen band of σ. One model call per step, because the corrector reuses the prediction at the predicted state. The node lets the band and orders be set.

entries.name: SA-Solver PECE
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same solver with use_pece on: after correcting, the model is evaluated again at the corrected state and that replaces the latest history entry. This roughly doubles model calls. The name is a preset of sa_solver.

entries.name: SEEDS-2
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two-stage stochastic exponential solver on x0 in half-logSNR, from the SEEDS paper. Noise is drawn per sub-segment and the stage noise is carried forward with a decay factor, rather than drawn independently. Default phi_1, r=0.5. Uses plain seeded Gaussian, not a Brownian tree.

entries.name: SEEDS-3
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Three-stage version of SEEDS. It makes three model calls per step and chains stage noise across the sub-segments. Final x uses the first and third x0 predictions; the second feeds only the third stage. No dedicated node, so r₁=⅓, r₂=⅔, η=1 come from defaults.

entries.name: UniPC (B1, bh1)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Unified predictor-corrector working on x0 in VP coordinates. Each step's corrector call also serves as the history for the next step, which gives one model call per step at up to third order. The default bh1 variant uses B(h)=h with a sign flip.

entries.name: UniPC (B2, bh2)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same driver and code as uni_pc, with B(h)=e^{−h}−1 in the coefficients in place of −h. Same cost, one model call per step.

entries.name: VOID DDIM (literal DDIM, node only)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The only literal DDIM loop in core, written for VOID inpainting models that were trained in alpha space. It subclasses Sampler directly, so it skips KSAMPLER's noise scaling, inverse scaling and inpaint wrapper. It only makes sense with those models.

entries.name: AccelDiff AdaptiveDiff step skipping
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Forks core solvers and tracks mean absolute change of the latent per step. When the second difference of that change is small relative to the last change, it reuses the previous x0 prediction with no model call. A guard forces a real call after max_skip_steps skips.

entries.name: AccelDiff EasyCache solver fork
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Forks core solvers with an EasyCache state object that accumulates a predicted-change estimate; while it stays under a threshold, model calls return x plus a cached output delta. This is in the sampler loop itself, not a model patch like core EasyCache nodes.

entries.name: AccelDiff SADA step skipping
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Forks core solvers and adds a stability test: after each step it compares the real next state against a three-term predictor, and if a momentum indicator is non-positive it skips the next model call. The skipped call uses an extrapolated x0 or a Lagrange fit over stored x0 anchors. It trades model calls for approximation error.

entries.name: AccelDiff ZEUS step skipping
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Forks core solvers with a fixed modular skip pattern: steps whose index mod denominator is in a set trigger a skip of the next call, and the derivative is linearly extrapolated in ODE-derivative space. Real outputs alone stay in the history. It is schedule-based, not error-based.

entries.name: Adept ancestral solver
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler ancestral with optional time-varying eta, a phase noise multiplier, a modified derivative, and an adaptive noise calibration. Adaptive noise can restart the whole run once it has measured enough samples.

entries.name: Adept solver
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A deterministic multistep in sigma space with a compensated derivative history and an optional Heun corrector. Adds clamps on extreme derivatives, NaN recovery, and dynamic thresholding when cond_scale exceeds 7.

entries.name: Akashic solver
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Marked experimental in its own print. A sigma-space Adams-Bashforth step inspired by SA-Solver with a tau-controlled noise, plus phase schedules for tau, eta and noise, a SMEA factor and a Native Detail Boost option. It is not the core sa_solver algorithm.

entries.name: AnyFlow Euler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler that also passes current and next sigma to the transformer via options, so a model conditioned on endpoint can use them.

entries.name: Bleh CFG-init sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs a few pre-steps scaled from raw x before handing off to a wrapped sampler. So it does extra integration with no model call.

entries.name: Boyo Experimental Richardson
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Named Richardson but runs a sampler, records every x0 through the callback, then blends the final latent with a weighted average of those x0s. No extrapolation between step sizes.

entries.name: CAB multistep (corrected Adams-Bashforth)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sigma-space Adams-Bashforth with variable-step weights, plus a defect correction comparing the current velocity against a linear extrapolation of history.

entries.name: CFG++ SDE family (ppm)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: CFG++ variants of 2M SDE, 3M SDE and 2S ancestral that are not in core. Core only has euler, euler ancestral, 2S ancestral, 2M and res_multistep with CFG++. They swap guided x0 for uncond in the derivative term.

entries.name: Clyb 4M SDE momentumized
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A DPM++ 3M SDE style multistep extended to one more history term, with a velocity blend applied to both the ODE part and the SDE correction term. It builds on a Perlin default noise sampler in this variant. Momentum smooths step-to-step update direction.

entries.name: Clyb BDF
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A predictor-corrector that uses a faux state at the lower sigma. Every step makes exactly one model call: step 0 calls at σᵢ only, and later steps reuse the prior x0 and call at σ↓. It averages two x0 predictions and then passes them through a scaling function; the projection and default atan2sin modes do not keep that average as-is.

entries.name: Clyb CFG++ sampler wrapper
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Wraps any KSAMPLER by proxying its model so the guided x0 is replaced with a CFG++ blended value. Any first-order sampler can then run a CFG++ style update without editing its loop.

entries.name: Clyb geometric extrapolation
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A three-evaluation single-step: evaluates at the geometric mean sigmas between current and σ↓ and extrapolates x0 to σ↓ with Newton divided differences. Three model calls per step.

entries.name: Clyb Taylor flow
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Multistep Euler in lerp form with a polynomial correction from up to 8 past x0 values. Coefficients come from a Vandermonde system in sigma differences. Includes four ways to split σ↓ and σ↑.

entries.name: CNS samplers
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler or ER-SDE where the re-noise term is shaped by a frequency gain table (gamma matrix) per step. Uses FFT with radial bins; the patch pack uses Haar wavelet bands instead. Different packs implement this for different model families.

entries.name: Composite policy for regional conditioning
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: When several area-limited conditionings are active, pi-Flow cannot average their outputs as tensors because each output is a policy. It keeps all the policies and averages their velocities at each substep.

entries.name: Cycle padding sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Wraps a sampler to pad the latent per model call inside a sigma window with a repeating size list, then unpad output. Possible padding modes include noise fills.

entries.name: DazzleKSampler RES4LYF fork
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fork of sample_rk_beta, longer by 231 lines. Differences not catalogued. See the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: DDRK flow-correct ancestral and restart jump
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Noise injection that respects flow matching, where the signal must be scaled as well as adding noise. On EDM it uses the usual split, and restart jumps reuse this same flow-correct form when moving up in sigma.

entries.name: DDRK HC2 and HC3 multistep (full read of hc2_step, extends ddrk-omega)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A one-call multistep solver in the same family as DPM++ 2M and 3M, with guards: the higher-order correction is limited elementwise to the size of the first-order move. HC3 adds a trust factor that shrinks the extrapolation when consecutive slopes disagree, and a free UniC-like correction of the previous step after the next model call. The code comments report a bench on an analytic mixture, not on images.

entries.name: DDRK Omega sampler
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: One sampler for Flow Matching and EDM, routing steps by phase: integrator choice from Euler, Heun, RK4, or its own one-call multistep HC2 and HC3. Layered with a latent fuse (SABER), ancestral renoise, restart inserts, sharpening and a schedule adapter. Auto mode tweaks params by step count.

entries.name: DDRK SABER2 fuse and perceptual sharpen
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two latent filters that run inside the sampler. SABER on images blurs flat areas of the latent with a 3×3 average, keeping edges. On video, it pulls unstable pixels toward a running average of past steps, not past frames. The sharpen adds fine and coarse detail back, weighted away from flat areas.

entries.name: DDRK step-count overrides
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Rules that change the requested settings based on step count and model family. Some of them run even with auto off, and the code prints a message saying so. Below is what actually fires.

entries.name: Detail Daemon sampler copies
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sampler wrapper that lowers the sigma passed to the model by a per-step schedule, leaving the solver schedule intact. Copied into several packs. The upstream ComfyUI-Detail-Daemon has no source in the library.

entries.name: Diffree dual latent Euler ancestral
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler ancestral on two coupled latents: main image updated normally, second slot replaced by its x0 prediction each step. Model-specific.

entries.name: DOGMA Klein samplers
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Six presets named for Klein base and distilled models, built from Ralston 2-stage steps, variable-step AB2, Heun corrector and direction limiters. REBUILD, BALANCED and DETAIL change where the expensive steps go. Gains and thresholds are constants in code.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M SDE GPU Sharp
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core 2M SDE with the same history scaling. Uses half log SNR and a GPU Brownian tree.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M Sharp
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core 2M with the stored previous x0 multiplied by a factor growing with step index. That raises the magnitude of the difference term late in sampling.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M, 2M SDE, 3M SDE with Dy churn
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core DPM++ multistep updates preceded by a fixed sigma inflation at each step, with no half-resolution call. The Dy name here means a churn schedule by s_dy_pow.

entries.name: DPM++ 3M SDE dynamic eta
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core 3M SDE with no structural change except eta follows a cosine anneal across the step index. Starts more stochastic and ends more deterministic with default values.

entries.name: DPM++ dual SDE momentumized
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core dpmpp_sde's two-stage midpoint with momentum blended into both stage updates, then a further 3M-style SDE history correction on top. Two model calls per step plus history.

entries.name: DPM++ Nm SDE (variable order)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Multistep DPM++ of user-chosen order, with SDE/ancestral modes, from a research repo about high-order collapse.

entries.name: DPM++ Ns (Chebyshev-Lobatto collocation)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Single-step p-stage solver: places collocation nodes at Chebyshev-Lobatto points inside the step, evaluates the model at each, and integrates the interpolant.

entries.name: DX policy (grid or polynomial)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The model predicts N clean-image estimates laid out across one time segment. The policy interpolates between them, or uses them as polynomial coefficients. It ignores where x has moved when choosing x̂₀, unlike GMFlow.

entries.name: Dynamic oversampling
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler with extra crop-level model calls at finer resolution on regions chosen by a high-pass FFT of x0. Each selected crop is upscaled, renoised, predicted at √2σ, and pasted back.

entries.name: Echo DMD Euler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Plain Euler in lerp form, no noise, with timing display.

entries.name: Euler A2
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Rectified-flow ancestral step that draws two noise samples each step, averages, then extrapolates the merged noise away from the deterministic base. The default extrapolation brings the total noise variance back close to one.

entries.name: Euler ancestral dancing
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An Euler ancestral step leaps to a sigma several steps ahead, then a second ancestral step with the same x0 returns to the next planned sigma. With eta_dance above 0, the split collapses: x lands on x0 and is re-noised to the next sigma, based on reading the code. One model call per step.

entries.name: Euler ancestral fixed noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core Euler ancestral with a sampler that returns the same noise on each call.

entries.name: Euler Dy
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler with noise churn-like sigma inflation, plus an extra half-resolution model call taken on a downscaled 2×2 corner lattice of the latent. The extra step updates one pixel of every 2×2 block only. It is a port of the A1111 Dy idea, with extra steps gated by index.

entries.name: Euler extended sigmas
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler that subdivides sigma intervals inside a set range into pass_steps linear substeps. So you get extra model calls at high sigma with a fixed schedule. Variants exist for ancestral and CFG++.

entries.name: Euler gamma and DPM++ 2M gamma
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Inflates sigma by a fixed offset scaled to progress, while the inflated value stays below sigma_max. Variants offer normal and CFG++ updates.

entries.name: Euler SMEA Dy
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler Dy plus a SMEA-style step. Same structure with two extra step types chosen by index.

entries.name: Flow UniPC (sigma space)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A simplified UniPC-style predictor-corrector working directly on v in sigma. The corrector redoes the prior step with a trapezoid of current and past velocity, using the current model call. So corrector and predictor share one evaluation.

entries.name: Flow-WLS
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Multistep with weights from a weighted least squares fit that discounts older history by γ^k, instead of exact interpolation through all history. The point is to limit weight growth at high order.

entries.name: FSampler skip by epsilon extrapolation
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Library copy keeps just the step file. Each solver step can skip a model call using linear or Richardson extrapolation of epsilon history, plus a learned scale.

entries.name: Gen2 soft denoise around LanPaint
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Wraps the LanPaint sampler so it can use a soft mask, since LanPaint itself binarises the denoise mask at 0.5. The wrapper blends the input toward a noised reference before the call, and blends the output toward a reference after. The reference can be the source, the latest generated output, or an EMA of generated outputs.

entries.name: GMFlow policy
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The model predicts a Gaussian mixture over the clean image at the start of the step. At any later point the policy works out the mean of that mixture given where the latent has moved, then turns it into a velocity. So the policy adapts as it integrates, at no model cost.

entries.name: Gradual Latent sampling
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core-style ancestral, 2M SDE and LCM loops that upscale the latent between start_step and end_step in stages, with an optional unsharp mask. The model sees growing resolution as sampling goes.

entries.name: Inversed Euler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler walked up sigmas to recover noise from a latent. Two packs differ: Easy-Use divides by 2σ on step 1 and returns x/σ_last; the other offers fixed-point refinement.

entries.name: Iterative mixing sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Per-step blending of denoised latent with a pre-noised copy of a source latent by a schedule.

entries.name: jankdiffusehigh
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Sampler object doing a HiDiffusion-like staged high-resolution run. Only the entry wrapper was read.

entries.name: Kohaku LoNyu Yog
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An Euler ancestral variant that for the first half of the steps also evaluates the model at the negated latent, averages derivatives, then does a third evaluation. It costs 3 calls per step in that half and 1 afterwards.

entries.name: LanPaint inner early stop
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Ends the inner relaxation of one outer step once the predicted image inside the mask stops changing. It watches the unknown area and a one-pixel ring next to the kept area, and also checks that many small changes have not added up to a large drift. Off by default: the nodes set the threshold to 0.0.

entries.name: LanPaint Langevin inpaint
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Inpainting sampler that does Langevin inner steps per step inside the mask. A thinking loop with friction.

entries.name: LanPaint overdamped inner loop (full read, replaces name-level lanpaint-langevin)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Before each outer sampler step, LanPaint runs a few inner steps of a noisy relaxation over the whole latent, so the masked area and the kept area can agree before the outer step moves on. The kept region is pulled toward the source image and also nudged by a second guided prediction, the "BIG" one. The code uses an exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck step, the overdamped limit; the second-order damped oscillator is commented out.

entries.name: LC Speed Boost half-size steps
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs early steps of a flow sample on a half-size latent, then grows and continues at full size. Disabled on masks or low-noise starts per printed reasons.

entries.name: LC123 detail daemon variant
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Own form of Detail Daemon with a peak-shaped amount.

entries.name: LCM alternative family
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: LCM steps replaced by Euler-like steps on a schedule list. lcm_alt uses Euler for the first N, lcm_cycle cycles Euler and LCM, with optional sigma reordering. The ancestral option mixes predicted and fresh noise.

entries.name: LCM dual noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Blends two x0 predictions per step: the normal one, and one from re-noising an earlier x0 at the same sigma with fresh noise. That earlier x0 is this step's by default and the previous step's in parallel mode. Optional pre-normalization loops at max sigma.

entries.name: LCM eta noise interpolation
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: LCM generic step where eta interpolates between predicted noise (DDIM-like at 0) and fresh noise (LCM at 1). The pack comment says this is not mathematically correct.

entries.name: LCM parallel geometric median
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs several noisy copies at the same sigma and merges their x0 predictions with a geometric median. A robust aggregate for one step, at K model calls per step.

entries.name: LCM rCFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: LCM with a CFG computed from a stored reference: the unconditional is taken once from the first step or from an original latent. Reduces calls versus standard CFG.

entries.name: LCM TTM JVP
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Discards x for x0 as LCM does, re-noises to the next sigma, takes a JVP there, and applies a second-order correction before re-noising again. Two noise draws per step.

entries.name: Lying sigma sampler variants
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Wraps any sampler so the model is told a slightly different sigma inside a range, while the solver keeps the true one. These forks change how the factor is computed. Core has LyingSigmaSampler; these add options.

entries.name: MD AMED sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Named AMED but the code is Heun with a sigma-weighted blend of derivatives, not an AMED midpoint network.

entries.name: MiniMax H3 Turbo sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler using audio and video schedules, separately or combined depending on the model sampling. On split shapes it advances video and audio with their own sigmas.

entries.name: Mirror Correction Euler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same family as Kohaku Yog: in an early phase it evaluates at a reflected state and at a point one averaged-slope step ahead, both at the same sigma. It reflects about the x0 estimate rather than negating the latent. Norm limits stop the probes from exploding.

entries.name: Neo DPM++ 2M CFG++ with flow branch
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Neo-Sampler's 2M CFG++ adds a separate branch for CONST model sampling, which core 2M CFG++ does not have. Otherwise close to the core form.

entries.name: pi-Flow outer loop and substep integrator (full read, replaces name-level piflow-policy-sampler)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A pi-Flow model outputs a small closed-form velocity function, the policy, instead of one velocity. One model call per step gives that policy; the sampler then runs many Euler substeps through it with no further model calls. The diffusion_coefficient setting optionally adds noise by stopping the policy short of the target and adding noise to land on it. It has no CFG: the guider is set to cfg 1 and only positive conditioning is used.

entries.name: pi-Flow policy sampler
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Model outputs a velocity policy, which is integrated with many cheap substeps per step without a model call. Default 128 substeps.

entries.name: PiD student SDE and renoise family
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Distilled flow samplers: take x0, then re-noise to the next sigma with fresh noise (LCM form in flow). No derivative at all. Variants add think steps and a creative start.

entries.name: PingPong sampler with FBG (MD)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: x0-renoise loop with an ancestral window, choice of blend functions for each move, optional restarts and feedback guidance using a log-posterior estimate. Core imports a compiled binary first.

entries.name: Q Euler ancestral with noise timeline
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler ancestral where the noise sampler pulls per-step noise from a supplied latent batch, so noise can be authored.

entries.name: Quantum spectral flow
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler/ancestral on x0 passed through frequency gating and momentum, a noise "resonance" step, plus optional Langevin correction with an extra call.

entries.name: RALU staged resolution sampling
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Two or three stage low to high resolution sampling for FLUX and SD3, with stage schedules fit by JS divergence.

entries.name: RALU three-stage mixed resolution (full read, replaces name-level ralu-staged-sampling)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Starts at half resolution, then upscales only the patches with the most edges, then upscales the rest. Noise is added at each jump so the latent matches the noise level of the next stage. This saves model time because early steps run on far fewer tokens. On Flux, the mixed stage really uses fewer tokens, with half-offset position ids; on SD3 it stays a full grid with blocks repeated.

entries.name: RALU-aligned SD3 two stage
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A simpler low-res then high-res SD3 pass that reuses the Flux Z value. It upsamples everything by nearest neighbour, injects block-correlated noise at the matching level, and continues with plain Euler. It can split across two nodes because the seed travels with the latent.

entries.name: REAL sampler (WeightFerry)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler with a look-ahead velocity at the next point; when mismatch is small it advances multiple steps using that velocity. If it stays at one step, the second call is reused as the next step's first call. Near the end it is plain Euler with no look-ahead.

entries.name: Rectified flow controlled forward/reverse
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Inverts then re-generates by blending the unconditional vector field with a straight-line field to a target, per RF-Inversion formula in comments. Forward goes to noise; reverse returns to a guide.

entries.name: RES 2S native (timesaver)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A clean second-order RES single step. Standalone formula, no RES4LYF import.

entries.name: RES 2S/2M without final correction
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A trimmed extract of RES4LYF default RES paths without the implicit final correction. Includes noise swap and rebound helpers and a 100-pass stage refinement. Optional sharpness.

entries.name: RES single-step momentumized
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Refined Exponential Solver, second order with partial step c2, with momentum blended into the stage and final diffs. Finishes with a denoise-to-zero call by default.

entries.name: RES4LYF legacy named methods
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two-line dispatchers: res_2m,2s,3s,5s,6s with _sde forms; deis_2m..4m with _sde. Catalogue entry only; see the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: RES4LYF legacy sample_rk
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Legacy RK loop of 483 lines. Catalogue entry only; see the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: RES4LYF legacy_sample_rk
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Older RK loop of 285 lines. Catalogue entry only; see the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: RES4LYF named methods
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two-line dispatchers: res_2m,3m,2s,3s,5s,6s with _ode forms; deis_2m,3m. Catalogue entry only; see the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: RES4LYF sample_common tiled
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Tiled sampling of 278 lines. Catalogue entry only; see the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: RES4LYF sample_rk_beta
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Main beta solver loop of 2172 lines. Catalogue entry only; see the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: res_multistep with churn
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A fork of core res_multistep with Karras churn added (s_churn, s_tmin, s_tmax), which core lacks. Most other functions in the file are copies of older core.

entries.name: Research DPM++ 2M/3M fixed
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A rewrite of 2M and 3M with explicit history lists and a separate 2-point warmup for 3M. Adapted from research-unipc-dpmpp. Optional sharpness on stored x0.

entries.name: Restart sampler (licyk)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same restart structure as Neo-Sampler; registered sampler.

entries.name: Restart sampler (Neo)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Karras restart: runs a Heun pass, then re-noises back up to a higher sigma and repeats a segment. When no list is given it picks restart counts from the step count.

entries.name: Sampler Adaptive step sizing
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Ignores the incoming schedule and picks sigma steps from the agreement of successive x0 velocities, driving any inner sampler one step at a time.

entries.name: Scheduled-eta SEEDS-2 and ER-SDE
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core seeds_2 and er_sde with eta computed per sigma by a tau function, by default active between 20% and 80% of the sigma percent range. Injection stops outside that window.

entries.name: SEEDS-2 Sharp
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core seeds_2 where the combined x0 has a sharpness-scaled term subtracted, using the same factor.

entries.name: Selective Sigma Detailer
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Detail Daemon idea with a spatial mask: two model calls at told and true sigma, composited by a mask built from the normal x0. So only parts of the latent get the lie.

entries.name: SelfRefineVideo
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler with repeated stochastic passes per step on a step map. Each extra pass re-noises from previous x0 at the same sigma, with an uncertainty mask taken from x0 difference. Handles combined video+audio latent.

entries.name: Sonar momentum samplers
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler, Euler A and DPM++ SDE with a blended history of derivative or x0, configurable by mode and a separate history rate. Optional guidance toward a reference latent.

entries.name: Sonar noise-override sampler wrapper
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Wraps a sampler, injects a custom noise sampler if it accepts noise_sampler via signature inspection.

entries.name: SPEED multi-scale sampling
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Starts sampling at a low-resolution DCT crop of the latent and at chosen sigmas expands to higher resolution with a spectral method, realigning sigma. Transitions are found by a delta rule from a fitted power spectrum, or given manually. Reduces latent size during early steps.

entries.name: SUN samplers (scaled uniform noise)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Eight core ancestral and SDE solvers re-issued with a uniform noise source scaled by sigma_down, single or multi-resolution. Seed is shifted per sigma. The SDE versions also keep a Brownian noise sampler and choose between.

entries.name: SUPREME multi-method sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A configurable loop: pick a step method per substep (euler, dpm_1s/2s/3s, rk4, reversible Heun, RKF45, Bogacki-Shampine, trapezoidal, RES, dynamic or adaptive order), plus denoised enhancements and noise modulation. It averages substep results with weights. It auto-disables noise on flow schedules.

entries.name: SUPREME substep and enhancement details (extends supreme-sampler)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Details the first pass left out, from a full read of the function up to the final step cases. Substeps all restart from the same x and are averaged, so they only differ through the history term or a differing substep method. The denoised enhancement runs inside every model call, including RK stages, with strength divided by the expected calls per step.

entries.name: TBG Flux2 mask sampler
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Flux2 Euler loop with own mask handling. Falls back to core Euler when no mask.

entries.name: TCD (alpha-table form)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Trajectory consistency sampling written with an alpha table computed in the node. Rescales the x0 and predicted noise by alpha sqrt values at the next step and renoises by eta.

entries.name: TCD (DDPM-step form)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Written as a VP DDPM posterior step using noise estimate and alpha ratio. Called TCD and takes a gamma, but gamma only toggles noise on or off here.

entries.name: TCD Euler ancestral
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Euler ancestral where σ↓ comes from scaling the timestep by (1−γ) instead of the usual ancestral formula. Larger gamma means bigger noise replacement.

entries.name: TDNodes resumable k-diffusion fork
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fork of older core k-diffusion where each solver takes a SamplingConfig that holds extra args, callback and a cache. History like old_denoised and denoised_1 is fetched and stored there, so a sampling run can stop and resume across calls.

entries.name: Timesaver inpaint think sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Before each step in the mask region it repeats think_steps re-noising loops mixing old and fresh eps, then proceeds with a step.

entries.name: Truncated Taylor method (JVP)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Second-order truncated Taylor method: it takes the total derivative of the denoiser along the trajectory with forward-mode autodiff, instead of a second model call or history. Same formula as the k-diffusion TTM idea. Needs a model that supports torch.func.jvp.

entries.name: TwinFlow unified sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A one-step style model loop that predicts x₀ and noise at once, then re-noises fully with fresh noise, as consistency sampling does. The model also gets a target time. The node keeps only the length of the sigmas it is given: the pack rebuilds its own schedule, using the official preset per the comment.

entries.name: VEnhancer SDEdit solvers
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Standalone heun and 2M SDE using c_in scaling and handling σ=inf at the first step. Used by a wrapper model.

entries.name: Align Your Steps (AYS)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Uses NVIDIA's published 10-step tables for SD1, SDXL and SVD (the file header links the source page), and log-linearly resamples them for any other step count. The denoise behaviour differs from BasicScheduler: it keeps only the last round(steps·denoise) steps rather than stretching to preserve the step count.

entries.name: BasicScheduler / KSampler denoise truncation
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: How partial denoise works for named schedulers: compute a longer schedule and keep only its tail, so the model still runs the requested number of steps at lower noise.

entries.name: beta
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Picks table indices from the inverse CDF of a Beta distribution, per the code comment on arXiv 2407.12173. With the default α=β=0.6 the indices pile up near both ends, so steps are small at high and low noise and fast in the middle. Indices are rounded to integers and repeats are removed.

entries.name: ddim_uniform
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: DDIM-style stride through the model's sigma table: integer stride from index 1 upward, then reversed, with a 0 at the end. Because the walk starts at the bottom and stops wherever the stride ends, the top sigma is usually not the model's sigma_max.

entries.name: Discard penultimate sigma (KSampler rule)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: For dpm_2, dpm_2_ancestral, uni_pc and uni_pc_bh2, KSampler builds the schedule with one more step and removes the second-to-last sigma, so the last jump goes straight to 0. This is an automatic shaper tied to the sampler name; a SamplerCustom workflow with its own sigmas does not get it.

entries.name: exponential
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sigmas evenly spaced in log sigma between the model's range, then zero. Karras with ρ→∞ in the limit; the plainest noise-level spacing and the one log-SNR solvers take equal steps on.

entries.name: ExtendIntermediateSigmas
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Inserts extra sigmas between neighbours in a chosen sigma range, adding steps only where you want them. Spacing inside each gap is linear or one of two eased forms. The default end_at_sigma of 12 only subdivides the very top of an SD-style range.

entries.name: FlipSigmas
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reverses a schedule so sampling runs from low noise to high, which is how unsampling or inversion is done. A leading zero is replaced by 0.0001 so the model is never called at sigma 0.

entries.name: Flow shift (time_snr_shift, ModelSamplingSD3 / AuraFlow)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The shift used by SD3-class flow models. It bends the whole flow time axis so more of it sits at high noise; every schedule read from the model inherits the bend. Shift 1 is no bend. AuraFlow's node is the same code with multiplier 1 (the model's timestep is in 0..1, not 0..1000).

entries.name: Flux shift (flux_time_shift, ModelSamplingFlux)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Flux's table uses an exponential shift μ. The node computes μ from image area on a line through two reference points, so larger images get more shift. The table has 10000 entries and timestep equals sigma.

entries.name: Flux2Scheduler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Flux 2 schedule. μ depends on both resolution and step count using two fitted lines, with empirical constants written directly in the code. Above 4300 tokens only the 200-step line applies. The sigmas are a linear ramp through the same exponential shift.

entries.name: GITS
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Looks up a precomputed schedule by coeff (15 values, 0.80 to 1.50 in 0.05 steps) and step count (19 rows per coeff, for 2 to 20 steps). Above 20 steps it log-linearly stretches the 20-step row. Header comment cites zju-pi/diff-sampler gits-main. All rows span the SD1-style 14.6146 to 0.0292 range.

entries.name: Ideogram4Scheduler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Schedule from a logit-normal quantile: equal probability mass per step under a logit-normal, with the mean shifted by resolution. Clamped by a fixed logSNR range then forced to end at 0.

entries.name: karras
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The EDM schedule: interpolate linearly in σ^(1/ρ) between the top and bottom sigma, so steps bunch up at low noise as ρ rises. Only sigma_min and sigma_max are read from the model, so sigmas are off-table values. Available both as a scheduler name and as a standalone node with typed-in range.

entries.name: kl_optimal
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Spaces steps uniformly in arctan(σ), which the code credits to an A1111 webui pull request. Because arctan is close to linear for small σ and flat for large σ, the jump from the top is large and low-noise steps are fine.

entries.name: Laplace
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Places log sigma on a Laplace-shaped curve so steps cluster around exp(μ), a mid-range noise level, and clamps the result to the given range. Node only.

entries.name: LCM distilled table (ModelSamplingDiscrete lcm)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Selecting lcm in ModelSamplingDiscrete replaces the table with 50 entries at a stride of T/50 and changes the denoised formula, so schedulers now walk a shorter table. The prediction mix is a consistency-style skip and output.

entries.name: linear_quadratic
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The Mochi video schedule, per the code comment: the first half of the steps move noise only a tiny amount (down to threshold_noise), then a quadratic takes the rest. Most of the step budget is spent near full noise. The result is scaled by sigma_max.

entries.name: LTXV scheduler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: LTX Video schedule: a linear ramp pushed through the Flux-style exponential shift, with μ from token count. An optional stretch rescales 1−σ so the last nonzero sigma lands exactly on terminal. Tokens come from the latent's spatial and temporal size, or 4096 with no latent.

entries.name: ManualSigmas
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Parses numbers out of a text string into a schedule, with nothing checked: no descending check and no required trailing zero. Marked experimental.

entries.name: ModelNoiseScale
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Keeps the schedule and multiplies the noise inside CONST flow noise scaling. It rebuilds the model sampling with the same shift and multiplier. The tooltip gives HiDream-O1 values.

entries.name: ModelSamplingAV / MiniMaxH3SigmaShift
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A flow table for packed audio-video latents. The video shift drives the schedule; the audio shift is stored and sets an audio scale, and both go to the model through transformer options so it can derive the audio schedule. The vsaan212 fallback differs: it uses the plain flow table, so it stores no audio shift or audio scale and passes the audio shift only through transformer options.

entries.name: ModelSamplingContinuousEDM
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Continuous EDM sigma range with the 1000 point log-spaced table only for compatibility. Option list: eps, edm (σ_data 0.5), v_prediction, edm_playground_v2.5 (also replaces latent format), cosmos_rflow (changes base class).

entries.name: ModelSamplingContinuousV
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Continuous v-prediction with an arctan time map, plus a log-spaced compatibility table.

entries.name: ModelSamplingDiscrete base table + zero terminal SNR
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The sigma table every discrete SD-style model carries. It comes from a β schedule and is the source for simple, normal, ddim_uniform and beta. The ModelSamplingDiscrete node also switches prediction type (eps, v, lcm, x0, img_to_img, img_to_img_flow) and can rescale the table to zero terminal SNR.

entries.name: ModelSamplingLTXV
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same exponential shift class as Flux, with μ from latent size on a 1024..4096 line. Used so the model's table matches LTX video length and resolution.

entries.name: Name-only wrappers of core schedules (TCD, LCM)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Nodes whose names suggest a new scheduler but which call a core one. TCDScheduler returns core ddim_uniform. LCMScheduler returns core sgm_uniform, with BasicScheduler-style denoise.

entries.name: normal
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Spaces timesteps evenly from highest to lowest with both endpoints kept, converts to sigma, and appends 0. If the model's lowest sigma is already about zero, it adds a step and skips the appended zero so the requested number of real steps survives.

entries.name: Optimal Steps (OSS)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Hard-coded flow-range schedules for FLUX (10 steps), Wan (20) and Chroma (40), from the source named in the header comment (bebebe666/OptimalSteps). Other step counts use the same log-linear resample as AYS. The tables are absolute sigmas and the node takes no model input, so the loaded model's shift setting has no effect on them.

entries.name: polyexponential
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Exponential schedule with a power applied to the ramp, so the log-sigma descent is curved. ρ=1 is identical to exponential. Node only; not in the KSampler scheduler list.

entries.name: SamplingPercentToSigma / percent_to_sigma
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Converts progress percent to a sigma using the model's own mapping. Used for start_percent/end_percent style windows across core. At 0 and 1 the mapping returns sentinels unless the node's actual-sigma option is set.

entries.name: SDTurboScheduler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fixed ladder of 10 timesteps (999, 899, … 99), slicing a window by denoise and steps. It is limited to 10 steps, defaults to 1, and sigma comes from the model's timestep map.

entries.name: SetFirstSigma
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Overwrites only the first sigma. Replacing a low starting value with a far higher one is a way to start a schedule from a much noisier state than the table reaches.

entries.name: sgm_uniform
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Spaces timesteps evenly from the top to the bottom of the model's range using steps+1 points, drops the last one, converts each to sigma and appends 0. Compared with normal it never lands on the lowest timestep before the zero.

entries.name: simple
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Walks the model's own sigma table (1000 entries on a standard discrete model) from the top at an even stride and copies out the entry at the floored offset, which is at or just above the exact position. No interpolation, so every sigma is a value the model was trained on when the model is discrete. It is the first entry of the scheduler list, and KSampler falls back to it for an unknown scheduler name.

entries.name: SplitSigmas / SplitSigmasDenoise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Cuts a schedule at a step or a denoise fraction into a high part and a low part that share one boundary sigma, for two-stage or two-model sampling.

entries.name: Stable Cascade cosine + shift
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Cosine ᾱ schedule with a logSNR shift, used by Stable Cascade. The sigma table is present only so other schedulers work. ᾱ is clamped so sigma cannot run to infinity or zero.

entries.name: VP (variance preserving)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Continuous VP-SDE noise schedule from the score-SDE line of work. It takes β parameters rather than a sigma range, so the top and bottom of the schedule come from the formula and not from the model. Node only.

entries.name: Adept "AYS" SDXL table
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pack-labelled AYS table with entries for 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 steps, normalised to 0..1, scaled to the sigma range. The values are near-uniform and do not match NVIDIA's table in core; the docstring credits NVIDIA. Other counts log-interpolate from the next larger row.

entries.name: Adept Adaptive-Optimized
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A fixed weighted sum of four curves. Nothing adapts at runtime despite the name.

entries.name: Adept AkashicAOS
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Single curve: power-warped ramp plus sine bump, renormalised, and a limit on how much one step can shrink.

entries.name: Adept AkashicAOS Alt
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Stronger power warp and a tanh crossover. ρ rises at low step counts.

entries.name: Adept AkashicEQFlow
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Builds step positions from a density in log-SNR space, peaked near logSNR≈0, and inverts its CDF. Step placement adapts with step count. Code names EQ-VAE models as its target.

entries.name: Adept AOS-E
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Three-phase ramp, slower start and quicker finish than AOS-V.

entries.name: Adept AOS-V
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Three-phase ramp aimed at v-prediction by name. A square-root fast start to 0.6, a linear middle to 0.9, a cubic end.

entries.name: Adept Constant-Rate
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Linear ramp plus a damped sine bump.

entries.name: Adept Cosine
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Cosine ease of the ramp, slow at both ends.

entries.name: Adept Entropic
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Average of a linear ramp and a power ramp.

entries.name: Adept Exponential Tail
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Power ramp up to a pivot, exponential after it.

entries.name: Adept Hybrid JYS-Karras
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Log-space blend of JYS with a golden-angle-jittered Karras, weighted by position.

entries.name: Adept Jittered Karras
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Karras with random offset per step, then sorted. The random draw is unseeded in this function.

entries.name: Adept JYS (Jump Your Steps)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Hand-built timestep ladder in phases: 1000→600 fast, 600→300, 300→200 dense, then the rest. It is a heuristic ladder computed from step count, not an optimised table.

entries.name: Adept LogSNR-Uniform
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Called log-SNR uniform; with σ_max>1 it is the same curve as exponential.

entries.name: Adept SNR-Optimized
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Blends a sigmoid and a linear ramp in log-sigma space, which the code calls log SNR.

entries.name: Adept Stochastic
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Base ramp with random perturbation: Brownian, normal or uniform. Sorted, with a monotonic guard.

entries.name: Adept Tanh Mid-Boost
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Tanh S-curve of the ramp, normalised to the endpoints.

entries.name: AIToolkit FlowMatch Sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Rebuilds an ai-toolkit trainer's sigma list for inference, by a formula path or an exact path that imports the toolkit's scheduler if present. Config table per model holds shift values.

entries.name: Aligned Scheduler (AYS timestep indices)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Builds an AYS-style schedule from timestep indices rather than from sigma values, so it reads sigmas from the loaded model's table, with log-linear resampling for the step count. This is why, unlike the core AYS node, it does follow the loaded model.

entries.name: AsymFlux2 resolution square-root shift
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A flow schedule whose shift grows with image size, linear in the square root of the pixel count. Unusually large values: 17 at 1024² and 34 at 2048².

entries.name: Beta presets (beta_33, beta_44, beta_53, …)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core beta scheduler re-registered with fixed α and β values as named scheduler entries. Three of them also add steps silently before computing, so a 20-step request returns more steps: beta_32 and beta_43 add 1 per 20 steps; beta_42 adds 1 per 10.

entries.name: bong_tangent (RES4LYF)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two-segment arctangent-shaped scheduler registered under this name. Several other packs carry copies or rewrites. One-line fact only, under the licence terms for this pack.

entries.name: Boyo chaotic and non-monotonic sigmas
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Experimental schedules. Logistic map or Hénon map values are scaled and sorted into a descending list, or random bumps are added to a simple schedule so sigma rises at some steps. Seeded. Non-monotonic mode really sends sigma upward.

entries.name: Detail Daemon schedule
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Keeps the real schedule but tells the model the sigma is a little lower than it is, by an amount that follows a per-step ramp. The model removes less noise than the sampler expects, leaving more fine texture. Its ramp is a separate schedule: rises to a peak at bias between start and end, then falls. The original ComfyUI-Detail-Daemon pack has no source in the library; this is read from copies in other packs (compared by reading one, not diffed).

entries.name: Dual Ease Cosine and Power Ease
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Easing curves in plain sigma. Dual ease raises a cosine to a power that drifts across the run. Power ease is a simple power of the ramp. Both enforce a small minimum gap.

entries.name: Dynamic Sigma Scheduler (no-model re-derivation)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reimplements core schedulers and model sigma tables from scratch for a named profile, so a schedule can be previewed without loading a model. Adds a rescale to user start and end sigmas, a curve factor, and per-step manual edits.

entries.name: EA Lightning motion bias
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pairs of power curves with a bias input mapping to the exponent. Hold high lingers at high noise, and big drop falls early. Forced to run from 1 to 0 and rounded to five decimals.

entries.name: Echo DMD sigmas + conditioning remap
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sigmas at preset points for a DMD-trained model, plus a node that rewrites a sigma list. Nearest snaps each value to the closest trained anchor. Interpolated returns the value unchanged inside the anchor range, because its lerp cancels out. The sampler uses one sigma for both model and step, so step size and conditioning are not decoupled, despite the docstring.

entries.name: Fixed-shift flow one-liners (Iris, LLaDA turbo, Bernini, DMAD, AsymFlux2)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Many model packs write the same ramp-through-flow-shift formula with their own fixed shift, or a small variation at the top end. Listed once. Differences are the shift value, the starting t, and whether a zero is appended.

entries.name: FlowMatch Scheduler (ai-toolkit style, with random types)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Multi-mode scheduler: linear, shift, shift_exponential, flux_shift with resolution μ, plus sigmoid and lognorm_blend types whose sigmas are random draws that get sorted. Those two types mirror training timestep sampling and change per run. Options add bell-curve weighting and terminal stretch.

entries.name: FlowMatch scheduler (DiffSynth-style)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Linear sigmas from a denoise-scaled start, bent by the flow shift. Options match a training-repo scheduler: inverse, extra_one_step (drops the last point) and reverse. No 0 is ever appended: with extra_one_step off the list ends at the shifted sigma_min.

entries.name: FlowMatchEulerDiscrete wrapper (diffusers)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Exposes diffusers' FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler config as a node and registers scheduler names. Math is inside the diffusers library, which this pack calls; not read here. Pack's vq_diffusion handler returns a plain linear ramp.

entries.name: Gaussian Tail Scheduler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Uses the normal distribution's tail to fall from sigmax down to sigmin, with a very fast early drop and a long flat tail near sigmin.

entries.name: GR sigma presets (Z-Image lists)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Hand-written lists by step count and named presets, returned with zone metadata.

entries.name: H3 held-join second-pass preset
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A fixed four-step schedule offered for the second pass of a continued H3 scene. It starts at half noise rather than at one, and it sits next to a held video prefix and frozen audio in the node's latent output. The user can edit the string.

entries.name: H3 PDD 8-step simple grid
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The schedule official H3 Acc PDD files are checked against: eight uniform steps before the H3 video shift. This pack's error text asks for 8 steps, simple, denoise 1 and shift 12/3, and it raises on anything else.

entries.name: H3 per-step audio shift curve
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Multiplies the H3 audio shift by a user-drawn curve over the steps. A flat curve at 1.0 changes nothing. It only rewrites the transformer option for each step and leaves the model_sampling object alone, so the audio carry scale used for latent in and out stays at its fixed value.

entries.name: H3 PTD file-defined knots
entries.label: from pack README claim
entries.plain: PTD files carry their own sigma knots, and the node returns them as a SIGMAS output. Node text gives a Ref2VA grid starting 1.0, 0.988 and an fl2va 4-step grid. Sampling off these knots raises an error.

entries.name: H3 second-pass staggered schedule
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Builds a second-pass H3 schedule in two separate moves. The starting sigma is copied from a known scheduler, step count and denoise recipe, then a shorter front-loaded curve runs from there to near zero, so the first step does most of the work of removing the upscale grid. This avoids swapping the scheduler name in a trim, which its docstring says reaches a very different start sigma.

entries.name: H3 v2v injection truncation
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Keeps only the tail of a normal schedule so a video-to-video pass starts partway in. The node calls this the quality dial of its pipeline and offers named presets. It is a step-count crop, not a sigma target, so the sigma reached depends on the scheduler and the shift.

entries.name: HyperFlow trained 8-step H3 grid
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A fixed, nine-point raw grid that the HyperFlow adapter was trained on, shifted by the H3 video shift to produce sampler sigmas. The file's own header can replace the grid. It is symmetric around 0.5 before the shift.

entries.name: Interactive and text sigma editors
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Nodes where the user draws or types the curve. The digest shows many of these; a few were read: a graph with points evaluated at step positions, a sigma editor taking JSON edits, a curve with point interpolation scaled by sigma_max.

entries.name: KoO Diffusion EQ
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Treats log-sigma progress like an audio spectrum: bands get dB gains through Gaussian windows, and sigmas are redistributed. Read to the window step only.

entries.name: LC Detail Daemon (modes)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A rewrite of the Detail Daemon idea with the CFG multiplier removed and two extra modes. In look only, the answer is rescaled back to the real noise level. In keep structure, it runs the model twice and only keeps the high-frequency part of the difference.

entries.name: Linear scheduler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Evenly spaced sigmas between two numbers, typed in. The end value is reached without a separate zero if it is set to 0.

entries.name: LLaDA-Image base curve
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fixed power-composition curve in flow range, written by the pack for that model's base variant.

entries.name: Lying Sigma
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Simplest sigma lie: inside a window set by start and end percent, multiply the sigma shown to the model by a fixed factor. A negative factor means the model sees less noise and leaves more detail. Actual step sizes are unchanged. It wraps any sampler.

entries.name: Manual scheduler (expression)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Takes a typed formula and evaluates it per step using asteval. Variables include sigmax, sigmin, phi, position y and x, normalised descending Fibonacci f, step j and count s.

entries.name: MD GITS "Boomerang"
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Labelled GITS, but it uses a tanh S-curve in log sigma, with no optimised tables as in core.

entries.name: MD Hybrid Adaptive Sigmas
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Single node with many modes, written as standalone formulas without reading the model's table. Several modes reuse core scheduler names for different curves, so results won't match core. Chunks can chain modes. The output usually ends at sigma_min, so a trailing zero depends on node options not read here.

entries.name: Multiply sigmas (uniform scale)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Multiplies all sigmas by one factor. The sampler then starts and steps at scaled noise levels, which changes how much noise is added and removed. Many packs reimplement this one line.

entries.name: NKD sigma equalize (measured)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Uses a measured quantity: how much the predicted x0 changes per step in a reference run. It then places new sigmas at equal shares of a power of that change. A schedule fitted to the model and prompt.

entries.name: Offset first sigma for SNR (flow)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: On a flow model, moves a first sigma of 1 or above slightly inside the range, because at σ=1 the flow state has no signal.

entries.name: power_shift / radiance_shift / inverse_squared
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Picks table indices from a power curve, with midpoint_shift warping the input. power_shift with defaults equals inverse_squared. radiance_shift is the same formula with step+1, a discarded penultimate and its own defaults. All dedupe repeats, as with beta.

entries.name: Quadratic anchor curves
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Hard-coded anchor sigmas for Qwen Image 2.1 turbo, interpolated piecewise-quadratic to any step count. Header credits ComfyUI-Quadratic-Schedulers.

entries.name: RALU NT-DM schedule fit
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fits per-stage shifts so the mixed-resolution schedule spends time where the normal schedule would, measured by Jensen-Shannon distance on a 1000 point grid. Used only when you give custom stage steps and ends; presets carry the fitted numbers. Needs scipy.

entries.name: Sigma curve from points (linear, PCHIP)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Resamples a list of control sigmas to any step count, either piecewise-linear or with monotonic PCHIP. Ignores the model's range even though a model is passed. Default points are hard-coded in the pack.

entries.name: Sigma merge / average family
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Blends schedules of the same length. Fixed blend, a per-index gradual blend from p to 1−p, or a mean of up to 25 inputs. Weighted scheduler mixing also belongs here.

entries.name: Sigma splice (sigmas_concat)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Replaces the tail of one schedule with the tail of another at an index. Its optional rescale multiplies by Σresult/Σσ₁, which pushes the sum further from the first schedule rather than matching it: matching would need the inverse ratio.

entries.name: sigmas_* toolbox (RES4LYF)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: A file holding 81 classes, of which 71 are named sigmas_*. By name they cover arithmetic, cleanup, splits, and shaping functions such as sigmoid, easing, hyperbolic, gaussian, Lambert W, plus exotic names (Collatz, Conway, persistent homology). These class names were read; the bodies were not. Short entry, see the tribute page.

entries.name: SigmasFunction (including plain cosine)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: One node with a menu of unit-range curves. It's where the simplest cosine and exponential ramps live, plus Gaussian, polynomial fit of points, custom expressions and a Qwen Image 2.1 option.

entries.name: SigmaWaveForm generators
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Generate a sequence from a sine, sawtooth, stepped, square or random wave rather than a monotonic schedule. Companion nodes do Fourier filtering, attenuation and a phase-locked loop on sigmas. Because the output isn't descending, the result only makes sense as an experiment or a modulation source.

entries.name: Sigmax model-aware profiles
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A large pack composing schedules from named parts (base grid, shift, terminal policy) per model profile, with strict validity checks. Base grids and shifts were read. Profile choice and turbo presets were read only for the LTX table.

entries.name: Sigmoid Offset Scheduler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Picks table indices along a normalised sigmoid. square_k sets steepness, and base_c shifts the midpoint. Node adds a start_sigma rescale.

entries.name: Simple sigma ops (invert, offset, scale to range, rerange)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Small transforms on an existing schedule. Note that invert here reflects values and is different from Flip.

entries.name: SparkDiffusion CrossDistill
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Hard-coded mid timesteps per supported step count, with the start derived from sigma_max. Unsupported counts raise an error.

entries.name: tan_scheduler family (RES4LYF)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Node forms of the arctangent curve, with one-stage and two-stage versions, sgm and pad options. Takes steps, slope, offset and range directly with no model input. Short entry under the licence terms.

entries.name: TBG split-aware detail enhancer
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A lie based on neighbouring schedule points, on every third or so step: the model runs twice, once at a sigma pulled toward the next (or previous) entry in the full schedule by a chosen amount and once at the true sigma, and the two outputs are mixed. Uses a split-aware step counter to keep the place across split runs.

entries.name: The Golden Scheduler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Crossfades between sigmax and sigmin using two powers of the golden ratio, in plain sigma space. No table walk, so it reads only the model's range. The sgm option drops the last value before the zero.

entries.name: TS Shifted Sigmas
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Takes raw few-step distill timesteps as text and bends them by the diffusers dynamic shift for the latent's token count, plus a final zero. Docstring says it was written for a Qwen Image 2.1 turbo LoRA.

entries.name: TwinFlow Kumaraswamy schedule
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Linear time warped by a Kumaraswamy function. With the baked-in (1,1,1) control it stays linear, so in practice this is a linear ramp with a large gap at the low end.

entries.name: Two-scheduler split (SimKarr, Segmented)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Run one named scheduler for the first part of the steps and another for the rest. SimKarr builds each on its own step count. Apt computes both at full length and joins at a split, smoothing the join.

entries.name: Ultimate Detail Sigmas
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Inside a centred window, warps step density and adds a boost to sigma amplitude, then restores monotonic order. Helpers were read by name only.

entries.name: WeightFerry TORS
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A precomputed flow table by step count, with step counts absent from the table linearly interpolated from the 30-step row.

entries.name: Zipf and Zeta schedulers
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Weights steps by a power law of rank, with the exponent drifting per step, and descends by the cumulative weight. Big early jumps and a long tail. Zeta adds path shapes for the exponent.

entries.name: Adaptive Projected Guidance (core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits the guidance direction into a part along the positive prediction and a part across it, then weights them. It optionally averages the direction over steps and caps its norm. In core it rewrites cond before linear CFG, so later hooks see a modified cond, and the result carries one more unit of guidance than the Sana pack: with η=1 and no cap, core gives the effect of cfg s+1 even though its tooltip says default CFG behaviour. The Sana pack returns x̂_c+(s−1)·g' directly.

entries.name: Basic Guider (cond only)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A guider with only one conditioning. Its inherited cfg stays 1.0, so the negative pass never runs. Used for models that embed guidance (Flux and similar) or for no-CFG sampling.

entries.name: CFG++ (sampler mechanism)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Not a node but a change in the sampler step: the x0 jump uses the guided prediction, while the re-noising direction uses the negative prediction.
