This lets it run at small cfg (the sampler's direction is not amplified). The trick is a post-CFG function that captures x̂_u and forces the negative pass at cfg 1.

core_ref.sampler_name: euler_cfg_pp, euler_ancestral_cfg_pp, dpmpp_2s_ancestral_cfg_pp, dpmpp_2m_cfg_pp, res_multistep_cfg_pp, res_multistep_ancestral_cfg_pp, gradient_estimation_cfg_pp

entries.name: CFG++ history sampler (cfgpp_ud10_ab)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A core-side CFG++ step with two-step Adams-Bashforth blending of the derivative. The step is built from the guided x0 and the negative's direction, then lerped with a linear-multistep estimate. An optional zero-sigma extrapolation adjusts the last step.

entries.name: CFG-Zero★ (optimized scale, core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Rescales the negative prediction by the amount that best matches the positive, before CFG mixes them. The core node has no zero-init of early steps, only the optimized scale. It takes no parameters.

entries.name: CFGNorm (attenuating, post-CFG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Limits the guided prediction's channel-wise norm to the positive prediction's norm, so high cfg cannot grow its magnitude. The strength here is a plain multiplier on the whole result, not a blend.

entries.name: CFGNorm pre_cfg mode (norm-scaled CFG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A second, separate behaviour inside the same node. It works on the noise-side difference, replaces the CFG line, and can raise as well as lower magnitude. The tooltip says it matches models like Lens.

entries.name: Classifier-free guidance (linear)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The default mixing rule every guidance scale in ComfyUI goes through. The model is run on the positive and the negative conditioning, and the result is pushed along their difference by the cfg number. At cfg 1 the negative pass is skipped unless a sampler or hook disables that shortcut, so the negative prediction is all zeros. A custom cfg function replaces the line, and post-CFG functions run afterwards on its result.

entries.name: Dual CFG Guider, nested style
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same three conditionings, but CFG is applied inside CFG: the first positive is guided against the second, and the result is then guided against the negative. It always runs all three.

entries.name: Dual CFG Guider, regular style
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two positive conditionings with their own scales. The second positive is compared against the negative by normal CFG, then the first positive adds its own difference from the second on top.

entries.name: Dual Model CFG Guider
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs the positive pass on one model and the negative pass on another. It is the core way to do CFG where the two sides are different checkpoints, and loads the second model only when cfg is not 1. This is a mix of model pair, not autoguidance by name.

entries.name: Epsilon Scaling
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Divides the predicted noise of the final result by a constant slightly above 1, to fight exposure bias. Applied after CFG.

entries.name: Euler CFG++ node sampler (core nodes_advanced_samplers)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An alternative form of CFG++ in core, chosen by version=alternative on the Euler CFG++ sampler node (version=regular uses euler_cfg_pp instead). It is the plain Euler step whose derivative is taken with the x−x̂_cfg+x̂_u substitution.

entries.name: FreSca (frequency scaling of guidance)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales the guidance difference differently in low and high Fourier bands before CFG, usually boosting highs. It leaves the negative alone. A center box is low frequency.

entries.name: Guidance hook pipeline (sampling_function)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The order in which all guidance hooks run for one model evaluation. Knowing it explains why a pre-CFG node sees different data from a post-CFG node, and why extra negative passes are skipped at cfg 1. Hooks reading the uncond output at cfg 1 get zeros, not the cond output.

entries.name: Latent Apply Operation CFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs any LATENT_OPERATION on the guidance difference (or on the only output, when cfg is 1) in a percent window, before CFG.

entries.name: LTXAV identity guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Encodes reference audio and adds a positive pass without it, so the difference pushes toward the reference voice.

entries.name: LTXAV modality guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A pass with audio-video cross-attention cut in both directions; the difference pushes the two modalities to agree more.

entries.name: LTXV Dual CFG Guider (video/audio scales)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Separate cfg numbers for the video and audio part of a packed AV latent. Equal scales or a non-AV latent fall back to normal CFG.

entries.name: LTXV Spatio-Temporal Guidance (core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An extra positive pass with self-attention disabled at selected blocks of LTXV. It uses a transformer option, not a patch replace.

entries.name: Mahiro (Positive-Biased Guidance)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Blends standard CFG with a pure positive extrapolation. The blend weight comes from how similar a compressed negative leap is to the merged result: similar means more ordinary CFG, dissimilar more positive leap. No parameters.

entries.name: Normalized Attention Guidance (core DiT form)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Applies a negative prompt inside attention rather than at the end, so it can work on models run at cfg 1. Core reads both cond and uncond tokens at each self-attention output, extrapolates, caps the L1 norm ratio, blends, and overwrites. Because it needs both in the same batch, it disables the cfg 1 skip.

entries.name: Perp-Neg
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Removes from the negative prompt's effect the part that points along the positive prompt, so a negative cannot cancel what the positive asks for. It needs a third, empty-prompt pass as the base.

entries.name: Perturbed-Attention Guidance (core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An extra positive pass with one self-attention block disabled. The difference between the normal and the broken pass adds structural guidance on top of CFG. The core node is locked to the SD UNet middle block.

entries.name: RenormCFG (Lumina2, core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Lumina's CFG: it splits off extra output channels, applies CFG only only below a sigma limit (cfg_trunc), and caps the norm of the result relative to the positive. At or above the truncation value, which is compared with sigma, it returns the positive only (the negative still costs a pass).

entries.name: RescaleCFG (core, v-pred and flow branches)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pulls the standard deviation of the guided output back toward that of the positive, counteracting the burn-out from high cfg on zero-terminal-SNR models. Core converts to v-prediction space for ε-style models, and has a separate branch for flow models that works in x0 space.

entries.name: Restore-CFG (core model patch)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pulls the guided x0 toward a VAE round-trip of the reference latent, more strongly at high sigma.

entries.name: Self-Attention Guidance (core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Saves the negative pass's self-attention map, blurs the negative's x0 prediction only where attention is high, re-noises it, and runs another negative pass. The difference adds guidance for the attended areas.

entries.name: Skip Layer Guidance (DiT)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An extra positive pass with chosen transformer blocks skipped, for models with no attention map to swap. The difference is added on top of CFG within a sigma window, with optional rescale. Uses the patch keys double_block/single_block.

entries.name: Skip Layer Guidance Simple (uncond only)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Does not add a pass. It runs the negative pass with blocks skipped in place of the normal negative pass, so CFG itself carries the perturbation. Cheaper than SLG, but gives no separate scale.

entries.name: Tangential Damping CFG (TCFG, core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reshapes the negative prediction so it lies on the main axis shared by the positive and negative. It removes the negative's off-axis part before CFG. No parameters in core.

entries.name: Temporal Score Rescaling (TSR)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales the score by a time-dependent factor r computed from SNR to change sample diversity. The result moves between x/α (no denoising) and the guided x0.

entries.name: Video Linear CFG Guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Gives each batch element (video frame) its own cfg: lowest for the first frame, full for the last. Made for frame-as-batch video models. It has no effect in a single-element batch other than using min_cfg.

entries.name: Video Triangle CFG Guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same idea with a triangle over frames: min at the start and end, full in the middle.

entries.name: "NAG" in output space (RT-RareTools)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Named NAG and citing the NAG equations, but it runs on the model's whole denoised prediction, not on attention. It is CFG with an L1-norm cap and blend, done over the whole image.

entries.name: "SMC-CFG" stateless sign bias (belgiangurista)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Labelled SMC but has no memory or sliding surface. It adds a fixed-size sign term based on current guidance to the noise-space result. The code comments admit it is an approximation.

entries.name: AdaMaG (adaptive manifold guidance)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Projects guidance on the positive noise estimate, weights the parallel part down, and schedules cfg by a power of t.

entries.name: Adaptive Guidance (cosine cut-off)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Stops CFG once positive and negative agree enough, so later steps save the negative pass. Decision is latched per sample.

entries.name: Adaptive Guidance guider with uncond-zero (asagi4 pack, patched here)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Measures cosine similarity of cond and uncond and turns CFG off for the rest of the run after it passes a threshold. In the CFG-off steps it can apply an uncond-zero style output. The patched copy on this box uses the least-converged image in a batch.

entries.name: Adept combat CFG drift
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Removes a share of the mean of the prediction, over all channels together, to counter colour drift. A one-line method inside the Adept sampler, called on denoised.

entries.name: Adept spectral modulation in v space
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reworks the guidance difference in the frequency domain before applying the scale. It is converted to v-prediction first, using the same conversion as RescaleCFG. Amplitudes in the top and bottom percentile of log amplitude are adjusted. Docstring credits ComfyUI-Latent-Modifiers.

entries.name: Angle Domain Guidance (ADG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Treats the whole latent as a vector and rotates the conditional by a capped angle, rather than extrapolating. The norm is bounded by construction.

entries.name: Anima adaptive CFG by divergence
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sets the CFG scale each step from how far apart cond and uncond are: larger gap, lower scale, then clamps it. The gap is measured over the batch as a single number, so one scale applies to the whole batch.

entries.name: Anima post-CFG utilities
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Three small post-CFG tools sharing one sigma-progress window. A frequency scale with a square low-pass box, a channel mean remover, and a noise add that rises and falls across the window. Names suggest model tuning; the code has no Anima-specific logic.

entries.name: APG Guider (rule-based, MD fork of blepping)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: A guider with an ordered list of rules: for each sigma the first matching rule sets cfg, APG scale, momentum, blend. It can run APG as cfg function or pre-CFG per rule.

entries.name: APG_ImYourCFGNow (noise space, adaptive momentum)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: APG implemented as a cfg function in noise space. Includes a built-in guidance limiter and an adaptive momentum that decays through the schedule. Projection is on the noise prediction, whereas core projects on x0.

entries.name: AutoGuidance + CFG guider (xmarre)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs CFG on a good model and a positive pass on a bad model, adding a capped push away from the bad one. Options choose the direction, a cap relative to the CFG update, a ramp over time, and how post-CFG hooks interact. Its paper mode mixes the weights instead of stacking them.

entries.name: Automatic CFG (per-channel range normalization)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sets a separate cfg for each latent channel so the guided output reaches a target intensity based on top-k value range. Also has a large set of extras: skip or fake uncond, experimental functions, attention modifiers, latent centring. It also replaces core's sampling function.

entries.name: Bernini chained multi-condition guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A chain of guidance arms, each compared with the previous one, instead of all compared with one uncond. Each delta can be APG-projected. In the T8 port the rv2v branch uses plain deltas even though the upstream mode has APG in its name, per the comment there.

entries.name: bleh block CFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Applies a CFG-like step inside the UNet on the block features of the batch, not on the output. Applied at chosen input, middle and output blocks during a sigma window. A positive scale moves the chosen half away from the other half.

entries.name: bleh contrastive orthogonal blend
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Extracts what is unique to each of two tensors by subtracting each other's projection, then combines the two parts with a base. A general tool that can act as CFG when a is cond and b comes from the difference. Only the first half of the 116 line function was read.

entries.name: CADS (conditioning noise, ppm)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds noise to conditioning tensors in a sigma window for more variety, then restores the mean and std. Runs before calc_cond_batch and works on c_concat and c_crossattn.

entries.name: CFG Megapack seven-stage plan
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A framework that splits a guided step into stages: when to guide, a weak branch, how to combine, where to guide (bands or regions), magnitude correction, an angle governor, and measurement. Each stage has a node that writes to a plan stored in model options; paper nodes write the same plan. All guidance goes through one runtime.

entries.name: CFG mixed with autoguidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits a total weight between CFG and autoguidance with a fraction a.

entries.name: CFG Three-Way Guider (separate null and negative)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A guider with positive, negative and a separate null prompt, running rules that core mixes up. negative_as_null reproduces plain CFG.

entries.name: CFG tied to scheduled LoRA strength
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Lowers CFG as a scheduled LoRA strength rises, for speed LoRAs meant to run at cfg 1. With strength 1 it reaches cfg 1. Optional hard switch to 1 after a step.

entries.name: CFG-Cache (FasterCache, frequency reuse)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Skips the negative pass on some steps: rebuilds it from the positive and cached frequency differences, separately for low and high frequency.

entries.name: CFG-MP / MP+ (manifold projection)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A CFG step followed by fixed-point iterations that make velocities match, with optional Anderson acceleration.

entries.name: CFG-OEC (orthogonal error correction)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Uses last step predictions to estimate error in the null branch and corrects it with an orthogonal term, when errors disagree.

entries.name: CFG-Renorm (megapack form)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Caps guided velocity norm to a multiple of the positive norm. Core RenormCFG applies this to x0, per the docstring.

entries.name: CFG-Zero★ (paper, velocity space, zero-init)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The paper form in the megapack: scale is measured and applied in velocity space, with an option to zero the first steps. The docstring contrasts it with the core node, which applies it to x0.

entries.name: CFG-Zero★ scaled (strength and scaled init)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: CFG-Zero★ in noise space with a strength blend back to normal CFG, plus an early-step scale that attenuates rather than zeroes.

entries.name: Channel incremental constrained guider
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: After CFG, decodes the prediction and takes the per-pixel change from the source image, keeping only its mean across RGB, so edits become grey-level and no hue changes. It is encoded again and pulled in with a strength that grows as timestep falls. Costs one VAE decode and encode per step.

entries.name: Characteristic Guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Solves a fixed-point correction at each step that needs several extra model calls. Falls back to plain CFG if it does not converge.

entries.name: ClampDenoised VAE round trip
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Each step, decodes the denoised latent to pixels, clamps to 0-1, and encodes it again. It forces the prediction into the range of the VAE, and costs one VAE decode and encode per step. It does nothing on latents that are not 4D, so it skips video.

entries.name: ClybGuidance (APG family with scale schedule and scalar projection)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: A Chroma-oriented APG with many options: uncond scalar projection like CFG-Zero★, a sine-shaped guidance multiplier by time, an atan2-sin mixed uncond, EMA momentum, and a norm cap relative to cond.

entries.name: Composable Diffusion (AND, NOT)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sums several conditions, or subtracts a negative with the null as a base. Differs from usual negative prompting by one unit of (n−u).

entries.name: Compress Guidance (CFG form, reconstructed)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs guidance only on some steps and scales it by the gap. Docstring labels this as a reconstruction since the paper gives only the classifier form.

entries.name: Concept Guidance (CoG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Uses a weighted mean of skip-layer predictions as a negative, from layers profiled per model and concept.

entries.name: Concept Removal Guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Steers away from a concept when a running score says it is near it.

entries.name: ContrastiveCFG (CCFG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales positive and negative terms by a function of their magnitudes, saturating them.

entries.name: Curved Rescale CFG (Raffle)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: RescaleCFG in v-prediction space with a multiplier that follows a bell shape over normalised sigma. Non-flow form only as read.

entries.name: C²FG (exponential cfg growth)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales cfg exponentially as sampling advances: base at high noise, multiplied by exp(g) at the end. Chains with a prior cfg function.

entries.name: DG-CFG (distribution-guided schedule)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A cfg schedule from VP scheduler quantities.

entries.name: DiffuseHigh wavelet guidance detail
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: During the guidance steps, swaps one DWT band of the denoised prediction for that of the low-res pass, normally the low band, and fades it out by step. This can run on image or latent, with the swap blended by a chosen blend mode. Extends the first pass entry jank-diffusehigh.

entries.name: Diversity boost
entries.label: from pack README claim
entries.plain: For distilled models that lose variety between seeds. In the first step it multiplies the raw latent by a random low-frequency field from 4×4 DCT modes, and across early steps it attenuates high frequency. Later steps get only the frequency part. Scheduling read from code; the DCT and filter steps rest on the docstring and tooltips.

entries.name: Dynamic Negative Guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Negative scale depends on a running posterior.

entries.name: Dynamic Thresholding (mimic scale, cfg_function)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs CFG at a high scale but renormalizes values to the range of a lower 'mimic' scale, to get a strong guidance effect without color blow-out. Has schedules for both scales and several normalization choices.

entries.name: Energy-Preserving CFG (EP-CFG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Rescales the CFG result to the energy of the positive. The robust default takes energy only from a narrow percentile range.

entries.name: FDG (megapack, with parallel and guidance per level)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Paper-form FDG where each level can have its own weight and optional projection. Differs from sd-perturbed-attention, which pins level weights to two values and voids the projection.

entries.name: Feedback Guidance (FBG)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Sets cfg from a running estimate of the posterior that the sample matches the condition, updated each step. Needs a state update after each step.

entries.name: Flux PAG and SEG (Fluxtapoz)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: PAG and SEG for Flux, with a mask, sigma window and rescale. Its base is cond, with two forms, depending on whether CFG is on. Partly read.

entries.name: Foresight Guidance (FSG, Spectrum)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Fixed-point iterations at mid steps that pull the sample where cond and uncond agree, then the normal step continues. Ported for Anima velocity prediction, whose docstring says it re-tunes the paper band.

entries.name: FreeU Advanced denoised stage
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A stage that applies a FreeU-like scale, Fourier filter and gain to the denoised prediction, for a limited number of steps. It works on the output, not the UNet features.

entries.name: Frequency-Decoupled Guidance (2-level Laplacian)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits positive and negative x0 predictions into a two-level Laplacian pyramid and applies a higher scale to fine detail and the normal cfg to coarse. Rebuilds the image afterward.

entries.name: Geometric CFG Guider
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Mixes two positive predictions by a weighted geometric mean, not a linear one, then applies CFG against the negative. Negative values make complex powers and only the real part is kept.

entries.name: Gigachad CFG rescale
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Cites the rescale paper, but the factor divides x.std() by itself, not by a cond std. So it is about 1 and the node does essentially nothing at any strength.

entries.name: Guidance interval returning negative outside (ericbeyer)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An interval method done by replacing the core sampling function, but outside the interval it returns the negative prediction rather than the positive.

entries.name: Guidance Limiter (limited interval, post-CFG and guider)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Guidance only inside a sigma interval, returning the positive prediction outside. The model patch still spends the negative pass outside the window; the guider version sets cfg to 1 so it saves it.

entries.name: Harmonic dynamic EQ
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An audio-style limiter and booster on the guided prediction, per element. Elements much larger than the typical block RMS are turned down, and very small ones are turned up. Elements in the healthy band keep gain exactly 1.

entries.name: HiGS (history-guided sampling)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds a high-pass filtered push away from a running average of past guided outputs, inside a time window.

entries.name: HiWave (wavelet detail guidance)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Guidance only on high wavelet bands; low band stays conditional by default. Only the combine rule is here, without the paper pipeline.

entries.name: Imagen dynamic thresholding
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The original form, for bounded pixel-range x0.

entries.name: LatentTools normalize
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Blends the guided prediction with a copy normalised to a target std, per channel.

entries.name: LatentTools orthogonal combine
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits the guidance adjustment into the part along the cond prediction and the part orthogonal to it, keeping the orthogonal part in full. Similar to APG with no momentum, but with an extra alternate-prediction term that can be included in or left out of the projection.

entries.name: LatentTools reference attention guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs the model on a noised reference latent to capture attention, then runs it again on the real latent with that attention transferred in at chosen blocks, and uses the difference as an extra term. The node is named DownsampledLatentGuidance, but the downsample code is commented out at this version. That makes it three extra cond calls per step.

entries.name: LCS latent colour space edits
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Converts denoised to raw VAE space, cuts it into patches, and edits those patches: by adding an edit vector for sharpness, or by intervening in a three-axis projection for colour. Then it converts back. Only the sharpen path and the head of the colour path were read.

entries.name: LF-CFG (low-frequency change-rate)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Damps guidance on low-frequency regions that changed slowly since the last step.

entries.name: LG reference feature injection
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: After CFG, pushes the output toward a reference latent with a strength that decays linearly over a window. Its direction is limited to three times the std of the CFG result. Named noise injection, but no noise is used.

entries.name: Limited Interval CFG Guider (cgem156)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Guider setting cfg to 1 outside a noise range. Its start and end inputs are fractions passed through the model's percent_to_sigma, despite the 'step' names. It does not look at the sample sigmas.

entries.name: LTX FDG (Laplacian pyramid, optional APG)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: FDG adapted to video latents, with separate parameters per modality and pyramid per frame, plus an optional APG-style projection. Partly read.

entries.name: MagicFusion saliency blend
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pixel-wise choice between two noise predictions by softmaxed saliency.

entries.name: MAMBO-G (magnitude-aware damping)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reduces cfg exponentially when guidance is large relative to the negative.

entries.name: Mimetic APG blend
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A plain APG blend for motion data, with the projection taken over channels and time. At apg_scale 1 it keeps only the orthogonal part, and at 0 it is plain CFG; between them it mixes the two.

entries.name: MixMod multi-model guider
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: A guider running several models with their own cfg and mixing outputs with team, FFT, depth-mask or other modes. Mode math in mixes/ not read.

entries.name: Momentum Guidance (MG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pushes the guided output away from its moving average over the steps. No extra model pass, and it reads and stores state through the model options dictionary.

entries.name: NAG for Krea 2 (float32 norm, prescale)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: NAG adapted to Krea 2 blocks, with norm calculated in float32 and scale, shift, normalization matched to the block. It uses the φ+1 form.

entries.name: NAG on both streams (Chroma, Clybius)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Applies NAG on the image and the text output streams of a Chroma double block, each with its own norm ratio.

entries.name: NAG text energy compensation (Donut experiment)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An opt-in step before NAG on Krea 2: scales the positive and negative text streams toward their shared RMS midpoint, so their energy matches before fusion. Off by default, and it attaches only to the model clone.

entries.name: NAG, ComfyUI-NAG fork family (φ form, parallel model classes)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The fork family keeps a separate NAG negative conditioning and swaps model classes (Flux, Chroma, HiDream, SD3, Hunyuan, Wan, SD) for NAG copies that run it inside attention. A CFG guider wraps this so the outer CFG can stay 1.

entries.name: NAG, method rebind (KJ Wan/LTXV, cubicj LTX2)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Replaces cross-attention methods on the model at load time. It keeps the φ form but limits via a mask, and can do the math in place to save memory.

entries.name: NAG, φ+1 form via attn2 (pamparamm, Anima)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same idea as NAG, but written with a different extrapolation, so the same scale number is one step stronger than in the fork family or core. The negative comes from an attention replace on cross-attention, and only the cond part of the batch is altered, with no second model class.

entries.name: NaiveCFG++ (as a cfg weight scheduler)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reproduces CFG++ on a plain Euler step by changing the cfg number each step, so any sampler can use it. The pack says it only matches real CFG++ with Euler.

entries.name: Negative attention (Extraltodeus)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds to attention scores a term from the difference between positive and negative attention. It uses a linear layer created on each call, so the projection is random and untrained.

entries.name: OTIP velocity guidance in RF inversion
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Used during inversion: nudges the velocity toward a transport direction to the target, with a strength by timestep, and optionally rescales by the velocity norm. Comment says it follows official code.

entries.name: PAG Advanced with adaptive scale and rescale (sd-perturbed-attention)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A fuller PAG: choose blocks, sigma window, an adaptive decay of the scale, and optional rescale or saliency fusion with CFG.

entries.name: Pentachoron rule (in-house, 4-simplex weighting)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An invented soft saturation: each group of 4 channels is projected on the 5 vertices of a 4-simplex, compressed by a softmax-like form, and returned. Small pushes behave like plain CFG.

entries.name: PerpNeg fork that projects positive onto negative (bvhari)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Early Perp-Neg node that removes from the positive its part along the negative. So it subtracts the projected positive, rather than a perpendicular negative. Name matches core but the geometry differs.

entries.name: Perpo Guidance (orthogonal part of skip pass)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A pack-invented variant: take the skip-pass prediction, remove its part parallel to the CFG output, and subtract the rest with a weight, then renormalize, with optional clamping.

entries.name: PLADIS (sparse cross-attention extrapolation)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Replaces cross-attention's softmax with a mix extrapolating away from soft attention toward a sparse map. No extra model pass, no extra sampler hook, and it can be combined with others.

entries.name: PMC-CFG (posterior-mean cap)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Caps the extrapolation so the result norm cannot exceed G times the positive norm, using a closed form for the largest allowed step.

entries.name: Power-law CFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A cfg that changes with the size of the guidance difference at each step. For α above 0 it is weaker when positive and negative agree and stronger when they differ; α below 0 reverses that. The space for measuring the norm is selectable.

entries.name: Prediction Boost (tmagara)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Adds an output-rejection term from the input latent's component orthogonal to the noise prediction, in versioned forms (24.03, 24.05, 24.07). Partly read.

entries.name: Predictor-Corrector Guidance (Langevin)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Conditional DDIM step followed by Langevin correction with a mixed score.

entries.name: Radiance "CFG++" cosine decay
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Named CFG plus plus, but it is a cosine schedule of the scale from cfg to 1 based on sigma. It has no connection to the CFG++ manifold step. It sets a single effective value for a tile, from the first tile sigma.

entries.name: Radiance energy-prioritized CFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Raises the guidance scale in mask regions and lowers it in others, using stacked masks with a priority each. On packed AV latents, only the video part gets the mask.

entries.name: Radiance SDR reference blend
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: For the first few steps, mixes the denoised prediction with a reference latent, decaying each step. It counts calls, so a second-order sampler uses up the steps sooner.

entries.name: ReCFG (rectified guidance coefficients)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Uses a pre-measured table of E[cond]/E[uncond] ratios per timestep as the weight on the unconditional. Needs an offline table pass.

entries.name: Rectified-CFG++ predictor-corrector
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A flow sampler step that evaluates the guidance at a predicted mid-point, with 3 evaluations.

entries.name: RenormCFGPost
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Caps the guided result's whole-tensor norm to a multiple of the positive's norm. It is the post-CFG version of the Lumina idea, without the channel split.

entries.name: RescaleCFGPost (x0 space, alt mode, window)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A RescaleCFG as post-CFG in x0 space, so no v-prediction conversion, with an optional alternative in which the blend weight depends on the std ratio.

entries.name: RescaleClassifierFreeGuidance (experiments)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The early version, using noise-space std directly with no v-prediction conversion. It predates the core node.

entries.name: Safe Latent Diffusion
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Steers away from a safety concept with element-wise scaling, warm-up and momentum.

entries.name: Saliency-adaptive noise fusion (SNF)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An alternative to adding two guidance terms: at each element choose whichever guidance has the larger soft saliency. It is a rescale_mode option for PAG, SEG, TPG, not a standalone node.

entries.name: SAMG (spatial adaptive multi guidance)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Per-pixel cfg, where high-energy guidance pixels get the lower scale.

entries.name: Scale-Locked Residual Diffusion
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Locks low and mid frequency bands of the noise prediction to a reference anchor, with a strength schedule, as a guider wrapper. residual_lock_multiband not read.

entries.name: Scaled CFG Guider (sign-dissimilarity mix)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Adds a part of the first-positive's difference to the second positive, scaled by how much the two disagree in sign. Partly read.

entries.name: Scheduled CFG guiders (per-step tables and curves)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: A group of guiders that set cfg from a step, sigma, percent or curve. They differ only in the source of the number, then call plain sampling_function.

entries.name: SEGA semantic guidance (megapack)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds or removes concepts, with a per-channel top-quantile mask, warm-up and momentum.

entries.name: SenseNova CFG norm cap
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Stops the guided velocity from getting larger than the positive velocity, either over the whole prediction or for each 32×32 pixel token. It only ever scales down.

entries.name: SharkGuider (RES4LYF)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: RES4LYF's guider. See the RES4LYF tribute page for details.

entries.name: Sigma-shift self guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs cond a second time with the same latent at a different sigma, and adds the difference between the two predictions. No attention is perturbed; the perturbation is just a wrong timestep. The sg_prev mode gets a similar term free from the previous step's cond prediction.

entries.name: Signed guidance (positive and negative from null)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Positive and negative pushes both start from a null prompt.

entries.name: Skimmed CFG (sign-masked fallback, megapack reimplementation)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pulls back only the elements where guidance would overshoot in the same direction as the value, using a lower scale there. The original Skimmed_CFG pack source is not on this box, so this entry is the megapack reimplementation.

entries.name: Skip CFG on first step
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Drops the negative while sigma is above a percent threshold, saving a call in the first steps. Core fills the missing negative with zeros and still applies CFG, so those steps return the positive multiplied by the CFG scale unless CFG is 1.

entries.name: SkipCFG Sigmas (aria1th)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Keeps CFG only inside a sigma mask and uses the positive prediction, or a blend toward CFG, outside it. The negative is still calculated.

entries.name: Sliding Window Guidance (SWG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An extra positive pass is run on overlapping tiles, not the whole latent, so the model sees less context. The difference from the whole-image prediction becomes guidance. Tile sizes are in pixels divided by 8. The cost is one model call per tile.

entries.name: SMC-CFG (adaptive gain, velocity space)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Keeps true sign switching but makes the gain follow the size of the guidance, to fight the texture chatter that a fixed gain gave. Built for Anima velocity prediction.

entries.name: SMC-CFG (tanh, blurred, noise space)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A smoothed version aimed at avoiding speckle: tanh in place of sign, a 5×5 box blur on the correction, and a K scaled down by √cfg. Works on x−x̂ divided by sigma, with a warm-up that returns cond alone.

entries.name: SMC-CFG (unit-norm, x0 space)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Treats guidance as a control problem: a sliding surface built from current and previous guidance error adds a correction before CFG. This version replaces sign with a unit-norm vector because the author says sign did not work.

entries.name: Smoothed Energy Guidance (SEG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Instead of removing self-attention, it blurs its queries. Blurring Q smooths the attention energy, and the difference from the normal pass is added as guidance. Blur sigma below 0 means flatten Q completely to its mean.

entries.name: Sonar reference latent guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Nudges the latent toward a reference latent during sampling, after shifting the reference to the current mean and std. Either a plain blend, or an Euler step aimed at the reference.

entries.name: Sonar wavelet CFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Performs CFG in the wavelet domain, so low and high bands get their own scales through a rule list. The low band and detail bands can use different blend modes.

entries.name: STG guider (Lightricks, pos-based with std rescale)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: LTX guider combining CFG and a block-skipped pass, then rescaling whole-tensor std. Core and pack differ in the base and in having the rescale. TenStrip's guider adds per-step CFG, STG and rescale lists.

entries.name: SuperDiff mix
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Mixes two conditions with a per-sample weight based on tracked log densities (AND/OR).

entries.name: S²-Guidance (random block skip, subtract, renormalize)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An extra positive pass with random blocks skipped, subtracted with a weight, then renormalized to the CFG output norm. The block count per step is random, and it supports many DiT layouts.

entries.name: T-GATE CFG gate
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Below a set sigma, returns the cond prediction with no CFG and caches attention, so late steps run faster. The attention cache part is covered by the patch family; this entry is only the CFG side.

entries.name: TBG scheduled reference nudge
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pulls denoised toward a reference latent inside a progress window. The comment states clearly it is not a real ControlNet, despite the file name.

entries.name: TCFG Advanced (blend and window)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core's tangential damping with a blend back to the raw negative, and a sigma window.

entries.name: Terminal-fitted repair of the guidance coefficient
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Replaces the guidance coefficient in the DDIM step with an exact-power one. Needs next sigma.

entries.name: Three channel CFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: CFG on the first three channels only, leaving the rest as cond. The function name is explicit, and the comment says this is the DiT/SiT form and questions whether it is a bug. The pack also has a rescale variant that blends the multiplier, not the output. OpenDIT also guides three channels but keeps each half's own remaining channels; city96's DiT port guides all in_channels instead.

entries.name: Token Perturbation Guidance (TPG)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An extra positive pass in which spatial tokens are randomly shuffled inside each patched transformer block. Like PAG but with no attention swap.

entries.name: Tonemap plus RescaleCFG combo
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Applies Reinhard tonemap to the guidance, then RescaleCFG on that result.

entries.name: TonemapNoise (Reinhard on guidance magnitude)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reinhard-compresses the guidance difference's per-pixel magnitude, so high cfg peaks are capped softly.

entries.name: Transition-point / opposite guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Tracks guidance norm across steps; before its first local minimum it uses unguided or opposite guidance, then normal CFG.

entries.name: TV-CFG (middle-peaked schedule)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Peaks cfg in mid steps, normalized so that the time average equals the nominal weight.

entries.name: Uncond Zero (Extraltodeus)
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Allows sampling without a negative: an output built from the positive and previous predictions, or an automatic-CFG path when a negative exists. Below sigma 1 it returns the positive alone. Partly read.

entries.name: VAGS (velocity adaptive scale)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Exponential cfg change based on how close the two velocities are, and the signal level.

entries.name: Wang CFG schedules
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A family of cfg shapes over progress: linear, cosine, inverse linear, sine, V, Λ, and a power-cosine. Docstring notes paper ambiguity on whether it multiplies w or w−1.

entries.name: Warmup Decay CFG Guider
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Above a sigma threshold, cfg follows a raised cosine of sigma, faded by a decay term; below it, cfg is constant. MegaCFG Guider combines this with others (not fully read).

entries.name: Weak-to-Strong segmented guidance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Uses normal CFG at high noise, then guidance from a weak branch at low noise.

entries.name: Windowed negative prompt
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Negative prompt only in a progress window; empty prompt outside.

entries.name: ZeResFDG (CADE 2.5)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Combines frequency scaling, CFG-Zero style uncond scale, and rescale, with an automatic switch based on high-frequency share.

entries.name: β-CFG (Beta schedule with gradient-norm normalization)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales cfg by a Beta-shaped curve over steps, and divides the guidance by its norm, so scale depends on the latent size and parameterization.

entries.name: AddNoise node (sigma span renoise)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Takes a NOISE source and adds it to a latent at a chosen sigma, outside the sampler. Lets you renoise a finished latent to re-enter sampling midway. Uses the span of the given sigmas as the amount, not the first sigma.

entries.name: BrownianTreeNoiseSampler / BatchedBrownianTree
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The per-step noise used by DPM++ SDE family. A Brownian tree gives noise consistent across different step counts because each interval's noise depends on the interval, not the call count. Makes SDE results converge as steps rise.

entries.name: default_noise_sampler (per-step white noise)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The per-step noise used by ancestral samplers. Independent Gaussian per call with a generator seeded once. Draws on the latent's own device, so results can vary between GPU and CPU; it also shifts the seed by one on CPU.

entries.name: DPM++ SDE noise term
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The 2M and 3M SDE samplers compute the noise term from the half-logSNR step, not from an ancestral split, and it scales with eta. The plain dpmpp_sde sampler is different: it uses an ancestral split in lambda space.

entries.name: ER-SDE noise scaler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: ER-SDE uses a nonlinear noise scaler function of the noise-to-signal lambda (σ/α) as a custom noise schedule. The noise amount is set by a chosen function rather than by eta.

entries.name: get_ancestral_step (VE ancestral noise split)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits one step into a deterministic move down to sigma_down and a fresh noise addition sigma_up, so the combined variance lands exactly on the target sigma. eta scales how much of the step is stochastic.

entries.name: LCM renoise with s_noise ramp and noise clip
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: LCM replaces x by the prediction each step, then fully re-noises it to the next sigma using the model's noise_scaling. This core version adds a linear ramp on the noise multiplier and an optional clamp of injected noise.

entries.name: Noise_EmptyNoise / DisableNoise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Returns all zeros in place of noise. Used to continue a partly sampled latent, or for unsampling flows; the sampler then starts from the latent unchanged at the first sigma (still scaled by noise_scaling with a zero noise term).

entries.name: noise_mask / KSamplerX0Inpaint (masked denoising)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: How masked sampling works in core: at each step the region outside the mask is replaced by the original latent noised to the current sigma with the same noise tensor, and the output is composited with the original at the end of each call. So noise is confined in effect rather than masked at the start.

entries.name: noise_scaling (how noise meets the latent)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Each model's sampling class decides how the noise tensor is mixed with the latent at sigma. This is where any custom noise amplitude actually lands. Variance-exploding models add σ·ε; flow models interpolate; some image-to-image model types ignore noise completely.

entries.name: prepare_noise (default initial noise)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The default starting noise in ComfyUI: plain standard Gaussian made on the CPU from one seed, so a seed gives the same starting noise regardless of GPU. With batch_index it draws and discards earlier batch items so item N can be reproduced alone.

entries.name: Rectified-flow ancestral renoise (RF variants)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Flow models cannot use the VE split, so core has a separate rule. It shrinks x toward the prediction, rescales up by alpha ratio and adds noise so the marginal is right at next sigma. Note the eta semantics differ from the VE version.

entries.name: s_churn (Karras churn)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Before evaluating the model, raises the noise level a bit by adding fresh noise, then integrates from the raised level. A simple form of noise injection on non-ancestral solvers. In ComfyUI it is 0 by default on KSampler.

entries.name: VOID optical-flow warped noise (core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Moves Gaussian noise along RAFT optical flow so noise sticks to moving content across video frames, for temporally consistent refinement. Keeps Gaussian statistics when pixels merge or split using regaussianize. Ported in core from R. Burgert's code for the VOID pipeline.

entries.name: 1/f noise with alpha, sonar (onef)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: FFT filter over height and width with the exponent as a parameter. Pinkish and greenish names exist as preset alphas, mix variants subtract two draws.

entries.name: Affine pattern noise (bias added to Gaussian)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Takes standard noise and adds a procedural pattern as an offset, then clamps to ±3. Pattern can be normalized first. Variance rises by the pattern's contribution, less what the clamp cuts.

entries.name: BFS shot-coherent noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Video start noise with several shaping options: replace coarse-block averages from a shot seed so shots match in composition, tilt the spectrum over space and time, and add pyramid. Uses careful unit-variance formulas throughout.

entries.name: Block-correlated noise for latent upsample (RALU, Pyramid-Flow)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: When a latent is upsampled during sampling, new pixel groups need noise whose average matches an existing value. Draws noise in small blocks with a weak negative correlation so that block means have reduced variance.

entries.name: CADS (noise on the condition, not latent)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds noise to the prompt embedding rather than the latent during the early steps, then rescales to original mean and std. Used for diversity. Stronger early and fading as sampling proceeds.

entries.name: Clip-wide noise sliced per chunk
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Chunked video rendering usually reseeds per chunk, so the overlap holds two unrelated noises for the same moment. This asks the NOISE object for one tensor for the whole clip's length, then gives each chunk its slice, so neighbours start with identical noise in their overlap. The docstring says this is what stops double exposure in the cross-fade.

entries.name: CNS wavelet-band colored per-step noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Per-step noise whose subband energy is decided by what the latent has already built. Haar-transforms x, measures energy per band, and gives more noise to bands that are unresolved. Total energy kept by RMS normalization.

entries.name: Coupled Initialization (batch repulsion)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Makes the noises of a batch negatively correlated so a batch of images spreads out more. First item is unchanged. Each marginal stays standard Gaussian.

entries.name: Cross-hatch power fractal (PowerNoiseSuite)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sums axis-aligned sinusoidal hatch patterns over octaves. The base class then applies color mapping and blur. The angle input is stored but never used. A structured, line-like initial noise rather than a random field.

entries.name: Custom noise from a latent (per-sample std normalize)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Turns any LATENT into a NOISE, normalizing mean and std across height and width for each channel and frame. So you can sample with hand-made or encoded noise and keep correct amplitude. Compare core's VOID Noise_FromLatent which does no normalization.

entries.name: DDIM inversion and sigma-reversal unsampling
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Recover a noise that reproduces a latent by running the sampler backward. Implementations either use a DDIM scheduler as in this vid2vid node, or flip the sigmas and let the sampler walk up, as in BlenderNeko Unsampler and North Noise.

entries.name: Detail Daemon family (lies about sigma)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Not noise injection in code: the model is told a lower sigma than the actual one, in a chosen sigma window, so it removes less noise than it should. Listed here because it is often grouped with noise tools.

entries.name: DJZ NoiseFactory plasma (image-space)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Generates colored images with OpenSimplex: plasma, HSV, turbulence, cellular and others. These are image-space only. To enter sampling they must go through VAE encode, then they act as a start image and not as a Gaussian-like noise.

entries.name: FFT colored noise, PowerNoiseSuite (blue/green/pink share one filter)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Filters white noise in frequency with a power law. Pink, green and blue use the same formula and differ only in default alpha, so all three reduce high frequencies. The result is rescaled to [0,1], so it is not zero mean before later steps.

entries.name: Flow renoise by lerp
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: For flow models: blends a latent with noise by linear interpolation at a chosen level. Matches the flow forward process, with sigma equal to the level.

entries.name: FSS noise (frequency soft-select, reference phase)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same core concept as structured noise, written independently: takes noise magnitudes and mixes phase from a reference with noise phase using a soft cut-off mask. Ref phase comes as a separate LATENT input from a frequency split node.

entries.name: Gaussian wrappers: scaled, diffusers parity, window seeds
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Small variations on core noise: multiply by a scale, draw on the GPU in bfloat16 to reproduce another pipeline's noise, or change the seed per chunk. They make no change to the distribution shape.

entries.name: Golden Noise (NPNet)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Passes the Gaussian start noise and the prompt embedding through a small trained network that outputs a better starting noise. Pre-model, one forward pass and no sampler changes. The network was trained at a specific size and token length, so the code resizes noise to 128×128 and handles prompt length.

entries.name: Green test and rainbow noise (sonar)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: FFT filter on the fourth root of frequency, then a separate std scaling. Rainbow is two summed green draws with weights.

entries.name: H3 AV add-noise for resampling
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Noises a finished H3 audio-video latent to a chosen sigma, so a later sampler can continue from it with noise disabled. It treats the two streams separately since the sampler carries audio at a different scale. It asks the model's own sampling object for the formula, and refuses σ = 1 because that path would throw the input latent away.

entries.name: H3 drift control: schedule-matched prefix noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A chained H3 segment normally keeps its carried video prefix fully clean, which the author measured as building up contrast and texture error along a chain. This changes the denoise mask each step so that the prefix takes a small, schedule-matched amount of the sampler's noise, fading to exact at the seam. The same mask must also reach the model, or it would label noisy tokens as clean.

entries.name: H3 EPS-style video noise scaling (monkey patch)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Replaces core's H3 noise scaling so the video stream keeps its full latent at every sigma, which leaves written transition frames in place as a start point. Audio keeps the flow formula, because code comments explain that its scaled signal would overload otherwise. It does this by swapping the H3 class in comfy.model_base, so it affects every H3 in the process.

entries.name: H3 reference picture noise setting
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Exposes core's visual-condition noise value, which sets how noisy reference pictures and pinned frames look to the model and the time label they carry. Lower means a tighter hold, and higher gives the prompt and LoRAs more say, according to the node's message.

entries.name: High-frequency noise re-entry on upscale (IAMCCS)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: After upscaling a video latent, adds only the part of fresh noise that the old resolution could not hold, scaled to the current sigma. Low frequencies, already decided by the earlier pass, are left alone. The noise generator runs on CPU, so seeds stay stable across memory modes.

entries.name: Inspire variation noise and seed explorer
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A1111-style variation seed with linear or slerp mix, batch seed modes and GPU noise. The explicit mask-free path of apply_variation_noise uses plain lerp with no correction, while mix_noise corrects variance. Regional versions apply it inside a mask.

entries.name: KJNodes generate and inject noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Simple generate and add nodes with options that matter: normalize by global std, average instead of add, optional sigma scale, constant-batch noise, and a final mix with fresh Gaussian.

entries.name: KoO pink, blue, high and low frequency noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Simple spectrum filter. Pink is one over root radius, blue is root radius, with a clamped floor for DC. Also blur-based high and low frequency variants. Values rescaled by filter mean, not variance.

entries.name: Laplacian, Student-t, distro zoo (sonar)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Heavy-tailed alternatives to Gaussian. The Laplacian adds a quarter of Gaussian so it is a mixture. The Student-t is scaled, clipped by quantile and compressed by a square-root. A distro node exposes 26 torch distributions.

entries.name: LatentForwardDiffusion (additive regardless of model)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds Gaussian to a latent scaled by the sigma from a chosen step. Convenient for renoising before partial sampling.

entries.name: LatentWalk norm-restored noise blending
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Blends two NOISE objects by addition and then rescales the result to the norm a single noise would have. This avoids the shrinking that plain weighted addition gives, which the code comment says breaks sampling. A separate random walk adds norm-fixed steps with momentum.

entries.name: Mix and spatially shaped noise (cg-noisetools)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Chain-style NOISE wrappers. Mix blends two noise sources linearly with a very small default weight, for near-seed variation. Shape multiplies amplitude across the image by a sine or triangle profile, so noise can be stronger at the center. Optional renormalise.

entries.name: Mix noise with renormalize to base std (allans)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds a weighted second noise to a base and matches result's mean and std to the base, within a mask if given. A safe way to do small variations.

entries.name: Noise rotate in the model noise coordinate (GTE)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Branches a partly sampled latent by rotating its implied noise by an angle, then rebuilding the state via the model's own scaling. Valid for flow and additive model types alike, since it recovers eps through a probe of noise_scaling.

entries.name: North Noise (reverse sigmas with injected noise)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An unsampler that walks flipped sigmas from low to high, but begins by passing strong Gaussian as the noise argument. It mixes model-driven inversion with an initial noise bump, optionally masked.

entries.name: Nukun recipe-weighted composite noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Named recipes mix Gaussian, blue, violet, pink, brown and pyramid with weights that shift by a detail bias. The recipes have family names, such as Illustrious and Pony V7. Result is renormalized. Spectral part kills DC.

entries.name: Octave-sum pink noise (MD_Nodes)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A 'pink' noise that uses no FFT: sums bilinearly upsampled lower resolution Gaussians with 1/(octave+1) weights. Closer to a pyramid than true 1/f.

entries.name: Offset noise (per-channel DC term)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds a single random value per channel across the whole latent. Allows much darker or brighter outcomes because plain Gaussian has almost no DC component.

entries.name: Orthogonal noise on rank-k conditioning
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Decomposes a conditioning matrix by truncated SVD, keeps the top components, and replaces the residual with fresh noise that is projected out of those components and matched to the residual's std.

entries.name: Perlin mapped to Gaussian by erfinv
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Makes one octave of Perlin noise per channel, then multiplies its absolute value by a million and takes it modulo 11, scaled to [0,1). That scrambles the field to roughly uniform values, which go through the inverse normal CDF. The result is roughly Gaussian in value and has little Perlin structure left. A min-max helper exists but is not called.

entries.name: Perlin power fractal (PowerNoiseSuite)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Classic 3D Perlin summed over octaves with an extra exponent on amplitude, then remapped into [0,1]. Used as initial latent noise or blended into a per-step noise.

entries.name: Pirog spectral and hierarchical noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pink, blue and hybrid filtering, plus a multi-scale hierarchy that bails out to plain Gaussian unless the latent has 4 or 16 channels. The hierarchical path has a final std normalize.

entries.name: Pointwise power-law remap (white, grey, velvet, violet, PowerNoiseSuite)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Despite the color names, these transform each sample's value and leave the spectrum flat. They change the histogram of the noise: with alpha near 0 values go toward ±1, with larger alpha the tails get heavier.

entries.name: PPFN Advanced KSampler (BrownianTree hijack blend)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Replaces the core Brownian tree sampler class during sampling with one that nudges the Brownian tree result toward a blend with power-law, Perlin, or cross-hatch noise. A way of getting any of those noises into SDE samplers. The nudge is small, 3% of the blend difference, and sigma tolerance scales the blend factor; 0 turns it off.

entries.name: Prepared noise tensor as NOISE (replay)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Wraps one already-made noise tensor as a NOISE object, so a sampler can be fed that exact tensor. The packs use this to guarantee that two passes share identical noise. These nodes only store and hand back a tensor; the distribution is whatever made it.

entries.name: Pyramid noise (multi-resolution, sonar)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds lower-resolution Gaussian noise layers on top of white noise with decaying weights, to give more low-frequency energy. Random downscale factor at each iteration. The most common approach to multi-res noise.

entries.name: RES4LYF noise classes (short)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: RES4LYF ships its own noise generator set for its samplers: colored fractal, pyramid families, Perlin, wavelet and more. Short entry only; see the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: Restart renoise for rectified flow
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A flow-model form of the restart jump. Variance-consistent because the signal scaling is included in the noise coefficient. Compare with the VE version in restart sampling.

entries.name: Restart sampling
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Periodically jumps back up in noise level by adding a large amount of fresh noise, then re-solves that segment with a deterministic solver. Trades steps for contraction of earlier errors.

entries.name: Same-color noise (cross-channel mean match)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Shifts each noise pixel so its across-channel mean equals the reference latent's across-channel mean. Carries a rough luminance-like map from the reference into the start noise.

entries.name: SeededDisableNoise (RNG burn with no noise)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Returns zeros in place of noise but advances the global RNG by drawing and discarding noise from a seed, which fixes later per-step randomness while the start is unchanged.

entries.name: SeedLab noise compositors
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A library of NOISE objects that compose: seed interpolation, weighted blends with renormalise, per-channel seeds, masks, tiles, frequency split, drift, and using a latent as noise. Makes each noise a plain chainable source.

entries.name: Shader noise source and staged injection
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Evaluates GLSL-style procedural shaders on the CPU as tensors (fractal, cellular, domain-warp, curl, tensor field and others), blends them with base noise, and can inject shader noise at interior steps.

entries.name: Short-distance noise (best-of-K minimum distance)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Draws K noise candidates and picks the one closest to a reference latent by squared distance. A cheap way to get noise already aligned with the image, in the spirit of minibatch optimal-transport pairing.

entries.name: Skoogeer latent procedural noises (std-relative)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds Perlin, simplex, Worley, fractal Brownian motion, swirl or reaction-diffusion patterns to a latent, with strength relative to that sample's std. Available in latent and image versions.

entries.name: Slerp, inject and unsampler toolkit (BlenderNeko)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A small node set for noise-as-latent workflows. Creates raw noise latents, interpolates them on a hypersphere, adds to a latent, and walks sigmas in reverse. Unsampler uses zero noise so the sampler's own solver acts as the inversion.

entries.name: Sonar noise framework (normalization and chaining)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A library of 30+ noise types with per-call generators, composed by chain nodes and usable for ancestral and SDE noise or as a NOISE object. It treats normalization as a first-class flag rather than leaving it to each generator.

entries.name: Structured noise (phase-preserving diffusion)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Builds noise from a reference latent: keep Gaussian-like magnitude from noise but take the Fourier phase from the reference at low frequencies. The result carries the reference's composition. Three ways to draw the magnitude are offered.

entries.name: SUNoise (scaled uniform noise)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Ancestral samplers that alternate Gaussian and scaled-uniform noise by step, plus a NOISE node for initial noise. Uniform range depends on sigma_down. Multires variant adds half-resolution uniform values.

entries.name: Temporal noise hold (AR(1) across frames)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Makes latent video noise correlated from frame to frame with an autoregressive filter, reducing boil. Each frame takes rho of the last one plus fresh noise weighted so variance stays one.

entries.name: TKG noise (color background shift)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Shifts selected channels of the start noise so a higher or lower fraction of values are positive, biasing the background to a color. A Gaussian mask keeps the center unshifted, so the subject stays neutral and the background takes the color.

entries.name: ULS empty-latent noise (colored, offset, fractal, character)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Empty-latent noise types with a cross-fade to white using the Gaussian sum rule. Pink, brown and blue use a proper radial filter with signed beta. The docstring acknowledges this has small effect at denoise 1.0.

entries.name: Uniform latent range noise (city96)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fills a latent with uniform random values scaled between measured per-channel limits for SD1 or SDXL. It is not Gaussian despite the function name. An optional shared random field across channels makes colored blotches go monochrome.

entries.name: Variation noise (similarity √(1−s²))
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Mixes a base noise with a variation seed so items resemble a base image. Uses the correct Gaussian sum rule, so the result stays unit variance, unlike many linear mixes.

entries.name: VideoNoiseWarp (Burgert, full version)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The fuller form of flow-warped noise that core adapts. Extras include degradation, which mixes warp noise with fresh noise by a variance-preserving blend, and temporal interpolation to latent frame count.

entries.name: Voronoi, Collatz and wavelet noise (sonar)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Structured noises that go beyond spectrum tweaks. Voronoi uses cellular distance features with many modes. Collatz iterates the 3n+1 rule across dimension chains. Wavelet builds octaves of filtered noise.

entries.name: Batch ops: LatentBatch, LatentFromBatch, RepeatLatentBatch, seed behaviour, Rebatch
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Batch management. The point of interest is batch_index, the list that controls which noise seed index each sample gets, so these nodes change noise as well as tensors. LatentBatchSeedBehavior "fixed" gives every sample the first index, so all get the same noise.

entries.name: bislerp resize
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Bilinear resampling where each 1D interpolation is a slerp of the channel vectors at a pixel rather than a lerp. It runs width first then height. Directions are slerped, magnitudes lerped, so per-pixel vector length is the lerped norm, which aims to avoid the contrast loss of plain bilinear.

entries.name: common_upscale and LatentUpscale / LatentUpscaleBy
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The shared resize used nearly everywhere. It flattens 5D video into 4D, optionally centre-crops to the target aspect, calls bislerp, lanczos, or torch interpolate, then restores the 5D shape. LatentUpscale takes pixel sizes and divides by 8 with a hard-coded factor of 8; LatentUpscaleBy multiplies latent size directly. No variance compensation for any mode.

entries.name: Core lanczos (8-bit PIL path)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: common_upscale's lanczos goes through 8-bit PIL images. It multiplies by 255, clips to 0..255, casts to uint8, resizes, divides by 255. That suits images in 0..1. On latents, which have negative values and a range past 1, it destroys data, so it is not a latent method despite being reachable through common_upscale.

entries.name: FreeU
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: UNet output-block patch. It multiplies half of the backbone channels and attenuates the very low frequencies of the skip features, at two block widths. Only works on UNets with model_channels. Family and hook details belong to the patch list; included here for the Fourier maths.

entries.name: FreeU V2
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Like FreeU but the backbone gain varies across the image. A min-max normalised mean feature map scales the boost, so strong regions get the full b factor and weak regions nearly none. Skip filtering is the same as V1.

entries.name: Latent add, subtract, multiply
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Plain element-wise arithmetic on latent tensors. Add and subtract first resize the second latent to the first with bilinear centre-crop and repeat it to the batch size. No variance handling, so adding two noise-like latents raises the variance and subtracting cancels content.

entries.name: Latent2RGB linear preview
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The fast preview. A per-format 3×C matrix and optional bias map channels to RGB linearly at each pixel. Packs reuse this kind of table to fake a latent colour transform without a VAE. It is an approximation fitted per format.

entries.name: LatentApplyOperation and LatentApplyOperationCFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A LATENT_OPERATION is a function value on a wire. Applied directly it maps a latent. In the CFG form it hooks pre-CFG and acts only on the guidance delta (cond minus uncond), then adds uncond back, so an operation like sharpen or tonemap affects guidance rather than the whole prediction.

entries.name: LatentBlend (core)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Straight linear mix of two latents. The weight runs the opposite way from what many expect: blend_factor is the weight of samples1. Only the "normal" mode exists and the node exposes no mode widget.

entries.name: LatentComposite with linear feather
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pastes one latent into another at an 8-pixel-grid offset. With feather on, it builds a linear ramp mask only on edges that do not touch the destination boundary. Corners multiply the two ramps, so they fall off faster than edges.

entries.name: LatentCompositeMasked
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Mask-driven paste. The mask is bilinearly resized to the source size and blended linearly at an offset, in place on the destination. Unlike LatentComposite it accepts negative clamped positions internally and a resize_source option.

entries.name: LatentConcat, LatentCut, LatentCutToBatch, ReplaceVideoLatentFrames
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Structural slicing and joining along x, y or time. LatentCutToBatch turns one long axis into extra batch items, dropping any remainder. ReplaceVideoLatentFrames overwrites a range of frames and refuses (returns the destination unchanged) if the source does not fit.

entries.name: LatentFormat process_in / process_out (model space scaling)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The scale between VAE space and model space. Base formats only scale. SD3/Flux also shift, Playground 2.5 uses per-channel mean and std. This is what "normalize" nodes such as the EmberFrame one reverse by hand.

entries.name: LatentInterpolate (direction-and-magnitude blend)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core's LatentInterpolate is not a lerp or a true slerp. It normalises each latent per pixel across channels, lerps the unit directions, renormalises, then applies a lerped magnitude. This keeps per-pixel vector length at the blended magnitude rather than shrinking it as a lerp does. This per-pixel behaviour holds for a batch of 1; the norms are taken without keepdim, so larger batches fail on broadcasting (inference from the code, not run).

entries.name: LatentOperationBlend
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Operation that pulls the latent toward a fixed reference by lerp, resizing the reference with nearest neighbour if needed. Via LatentApplyOperationCFG it would drag the guidance delta toward a latent, not the prediction.

entries.name: LatentOperationSharpen
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sharpens direction, keeps magnitude. It unit-normalises per pixel, convolves with a kernel built from a negative Gaussian with a compensated centre, then multiplies magnitude back. The result is not renormalised, so the norm drifts slightly.

entries.name: LatentOperationTonemapReinhard
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Compresses overly large latent vector magnitudes while keeping directions. The white point comes from per-sample stats of the magnitude map. It can go through LatentApplyOperationCFG to act on guidance. The formula always compresses, including at low values, since it is plain Reinhard with no knee.

entries.name: LatentRotate, LatentFlip, LatentCrop
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Lossless reordering of latent cells: 90-degree rotations, flips and slicing on the /8 grid. Values and statistics of the kept cells do not change. Flip naming is literal: x-axis flips vertically (dim 2).

entries.name: LTXVLatentUpsampler (learned 2x)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Video latent upscale by a learned network. It denormalises with the VAE per-channel statistics, runs the model, then renormalises. Keeping the model in raw VAE statistics is the point. Drops noise_mask from the output dict.

entries.name: PatchModelAddDownscale (Kohya Deep Shrink, hires-fix alternative)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A patch that does hires-fix style structure control inside the UNet. Early in sampling it shrinks the hidden feature at one block by a factor, and upscales on the way out to match the skip. Works at model feature level, no second pass.

entries.name: tiled_scale_multidim feathered tile accumulation
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core tile engine for VAE and upscalers. It runs the function on overlapping tiles and accumulates with a linear edge feather, dividing by the accumulated mask. Because the feather applies on all tile edges and divides out, this is a normalised overlap-add, not a seamless (circular) tiling method.

entries.name: 1D spectral blend of global and local features
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: rfft along dim 1 with a cosine transition, taking lows from one tensor and highs from another. Dim 1 here is a feature or sequence axis inside a patched module, not image space; only the function was read, not how the pack routes it.

entries.name: _slerp that assumes unit vectors
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A second slerp in the same Akatz file does no normalising. It takes the dot of the raw flattened tensors and clamps it to ±1 before acos. For anything not already unit length the clamp saturates, so ω ends up near 0 or near π and the weights blow up or collapse.

entries.name: AdaIN with a local window
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Mean/std transfer computed in a sliding window instead of over the frame. Fine structure of the input is kept while low-frequency tone follows the reference locally, so it acts like a low-frequency transplant. Uses OpenCV blur per frame.

entries.name: Adaptive difference upscale
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Blends nearest and a smooth resize using their own difference as the mask, so no VAE is needed. An optional step then removes high frequency near strong gradients, and a temporal EMA reduces flicker on video.

entries.name: altslerp (dim-selectable, colinear lerp)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: bleh's "slerp" blend mode. It runs on a chosen axis, treats near-colinear or zero vectors as lerp with threshold 0.9995, and keeps batch-of-t support. Code credits a gist by Birch-san. Only the setup part was read here.

entries.name: Attention-value FFT phase jitter
entries.label: from code
