entries.plain: An attention replacement that randomises phase in the FFT of the attention values, tilted by frequency. It belongs with patches by hook, but the maths is a frequency method. Fresh torch.rand per call, not seeded by a widget.

entries.name: BatchNormalizeLatent and normalize-shuffle
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Aligns all samples in a batch to shared channel statistics, for flicker across a batch. A separate node high-passes, z-scores and rotates channels (1,2,3,0), hard-coded to 4 channels.

entries.name: bleh scale_samples: interpolation, pools, biderp, enhance
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: bleh's resize dispatcher. Adds pools and any blend mode as interpolator, plus post-effects after a "+": FFT presets, kornia sharpen and blur, renoise. "random" picks a method each call, using the unseeded global RNG.

entries.name: BLENDING_MODES table (bleh)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The largest blend table read: lerp and scaled lerps, sign-preserving forms, inject, CFG-style, image modes, slices, probabilistic picks, cosine-similarity, orthogonal and wavelet modes. BlendMode can rescale t or normalise. BlehLatentBlend exposes all of them. Image-style modes are applied to raw latent values, so thresholds like a<0.5 have no image meaning there.

entries.name: Brightness, contrast, saturation on raw channels
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Packs that pretend the first channels are RGB. PPFN and Apt_Preset centre on 0.5 and use Rec.601 luma weights on channels 0,1,2, then reassemble exactly 4 channels. DenRakEiw centres on each channel's own mean and scales brightness by 0.5. None of this corresponds to image colour without a format-specific matrix.

entries.name: CampB latent op registry (unary and binary)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A registry of small pure ops used through nodes and an op-on-a-wire apply node. Most are one-liners: posterise, sign, soft-clip, signed sqrt and power, seeded dropout, min and max, centre. The named lerp overshoots outside 0..1 by design.

entries.name: Channel-space linear transforms
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Treats channels as a vector space and applies random but seeded rotations, reflections and shears across selected channels. Rotations and reflections preserve per-pixel energy, while shear does not. A statistics match step exists to restore channel stats. Experimental, mostly for controlled scrambles.

entries.name: Circular edges and seamless tile makers
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Methods to make the left and right edges meet. HYWorld blends the first columns toward the last columns and crops them away, for panoramas in IMAGE. Quilting offers latent seam makers through patch search. Content-aware tiles build Wang or dual tile sets for inpainting boundaries. Quilting and content-aware internals were read at node level only.

entries.name: Clamp and outlier limiting
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Limits extreme values. spacepxl clamps at k standard deviations per channel. valkymaera clamps to a fixed range. Sparknight LatentClamp does not clamp at all despite its name: it multiplies values outside the range by a factor, optional noise added, so it can still leave them outside. JTrigger Huberise keeps tails with a reduced slope.

entries.name: Contrast-limited detail boost
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Difference-of-Gaussians band, normalised by local RMS so flat areas and busy areas gain alike, tanh-limited, then gated down on strong edges. Passes audio of nested latents through unchanged, so it is one of the few that know H3 packed latents.

entries.name: DCT spectral expand upscale
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Upscale in the cosine domain: embed the DCT coefficients in a larger zero grid, fill the new high band with sigma-scaled noise through a taper, and inverse transform. It also rescales the signal and returns an aligned sigma, so sampling can continue at matched noise. Three blend modes; hard and linear are identical in the code.

entries.name: Detail transfer treated as a latent op, with clamp and raw tensor output
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Takes high frequencies from source and low from target. Built for images and applied to latents by permuting axes. It clamps the result to 0..1 and returns a bare tensor rather than a latent dict, so as a LATENT it is unlikely to work downstream.

entries.name: FFT phase/magnitude split and combine
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Puts magnitude and phase each into a LATENT wire so other nodes can operate on them, then combines with polar and takes the real part. Skoogeer keeps raw magnitude. CampB stores log1p magnitude as an option and adds swap, shaping and scramble nodes, but its core/freq.py is in neither the library copy nor the deploy backup, so swap and band formulas are not verified here.

entries.name: Five-band spectral EQ
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Radial Gaussian bands with gains in dB, applied in ortho rfft2, keeping DC unchanged and optionally restoring per-sample RMS. Written for noise, but the maths is general; noise family has the applied form.

entries.name: Gaussian low-pass FFT blend for dilated refinement
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Merges a low-resolution refinement with a full-resolution latent: low frequencies from the refinement, highs from the original. Cutoff derives from the downscale factor. Multi-frame video falls back to a plain lerp.

entries.name: Geometric median and spherical mean of N latents
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two ways to average many latents without plain-mean norm collapse. Geometric median uses Weiszfeld iterations and resists one outlier. Spherical mean averages unit directions per channel and rescales to the mean norm. Pack is a lab pack in the local library; core/freq.py etc. are absent from the patched copy.

entries.name: High frequency noise re-entry at upscale (H3)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: After spatially resizing video latents, adds fresh noise containing only frequencies above the previous resolution, scaled by RMS, so upscale stages do not lack high-frequency energy. Keeps old low frequencies untouched by construction.

entries.name: Hires-fix nodes as wrappers
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Most hires-fix nodes are compositions. OmniNodes calls core LatentUpscaleBy then core KSampler at a chosen denoise. Easy-Use's hiresFix runs a pixel upscale model through tiled_scale, rescales, then VAE-encodes. Neither has new maths.

entries.name: hslerp (lerp plus an offset on channel 0)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Lerp with an added term in channel 0 only, sized by the local difference norm, with sign flipped at t=0.5. The name suggests something fancier. bleh keeps three variants and its own comments doubt them.

entries.name: Hybrid upscale: nearest in flats, smooth along edges
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Takes nearest-exact as the base and bilinear on edges found by decoding through the VAE. The next entry does without VAE decoding. Costs a decode.

entries.name: Latent interposer (learned format converter)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Small residual convnets trained per pair of VAE formats, for moving a latent from one family to another without a decode and encode. Conversion is by weights only. Downloads weights from Hugging Face at run time when not local. The node offers v1, xl, v3, fx, ca as source and v1, xl, v3 as destination.

entries.name: Latent Normalized Lanczos Resize (decode, lanczos, encode, moment match)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Gets lanczos safely by doing it in pixel space. Soft-clamps outliers, decodes, resizes the image with lanczos, re-encodes, optionally mixes in a nearest upscale, then matches moments to the input latent per channel. Costs two VAE passes.

entries.name: LatentColorMatch via RGB colour-space conversions
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs kornia RGB→LAB or YCbCr or LUV or XYZ on the first three latent channels as if they were an image, without rescaling, then does mean/std transfer and converts back. Extra channels get a simpler match. Formally, RGB-to-LAB is defined for 0..1 images, so this treats latent values as out-of-range RGB.

entries.name: Lerp written into the input tensor
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Plain lerp, but written with torch.lerp(out=a["samples"]) after a shallow dict copy, so the tensor owned by the upstream node is overwritten. That can corrupt ComfyUI's cached output of the upstream node when another branch reads it.

entries.name: Manual format shift/scale (EmberFrame)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Explicit Flux-style shift and scale in both directions as a node, for moving between ComfyUI's stored latent form and what a Pi-Flow-like tool expects.

entries.name: Mean/std match per channel (AdaIN style)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Gives one latent the channel statistics of another while keeping its own structure. Many packs do this with small differences. The usual trap is reading argument names: in Tensor-Operations "source" donates statistics to "target", while the returned dict inherits from source.

entries.name: Min-max normalise and soft clamp
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Range matching rather than variance. Soft clamp pushes values back with softplus before an optional final hard clamp. USE_ORIG_NORMALIZE selects a global legacy form.

entries.name: Motion-adaptive latent sharpen and retime
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sharpens video latent frames in proportion to frame-to-frame change, with a fixed binomial blur high pass. The sibling retime node adjusts apparent speed by subtracting velocity from frames. Works on raw latent differences, not optical flow.

entries.name: Multi-threshold FreeU-style filter
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Extends FreeU's box mask in shifted FFT space to a list of (threshold, scale) pairs mixed by strength, used in presets for latent enhance modes after upscaling.

entries.name: Nlerp with lerped-norm target
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Cheap norm-aware blend. It lerps over the flattened sample, normalises, then rescales to the lerp of the two endpoint norms. Avoids acos, stays stable near parallel.

entries.name: NNLatentUpscale (learned resizer in unscaled space)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Learned continuous-scale resizer for SD1 and SDXL. Note the scale factor is 0.13025 and is set once for both versions. The bundle ships as .pt weights.

entries.name: Normalize video latent start (clamped stats)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fixes stat jumps at the start of a video latent by matching the first frames to the following frames, with the target clamped near the source so it cannot move far. Source stats are per frame over channels and space; reference stats are a single scalar over everything, so channel differences are flattened.

entries.name: NormalizeLatent to a per-channel dynamic range (only expands)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales a sample's channel so its largest absolute value reaches a format-specific constant, with the ratio floored at 1, so it can only enlarge. The constants are by format. Unknown formats pass through.

entries.name: OmniNodes blend with per-channel 0..1 windowing
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Image-style modes done properly for a signed range: each channel is rescaled to 0..1, blended, then mapped back to a's range. Strength multiplies the output, except in add and subtract, where it scales b. Lerp, add, subtract and difference stay raw. This is a different and more defensible way to apply screen or overlay than the raw-value tables.

entries.name: Orthogonal blend
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Removes from b the part parallel to a, then applies the blend, so t adds only new direction rather than scaling a. Options rescale to a chosen target, or dynamically fall back to the plain result when the orthogonal part would need too much rescale. This relates to perpendicular guidance methods.

entries.name: Phase mix on the unit circle
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Keeps x's amplitude and blends phase with y as a weighted circular mean, avoiding wrap errors of linear phase averaging. Bleh's fft_blend is a generalisation, blending magnitude and phase with separate modes, with optional shortest-arc interpolation.

entries.name: PPFN blending_modes table (bislerp that is not bislerp)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: WAS PowerNoiseSuite table copied into other packs, with image-mode names over latents. Its "bislerp" is a lerp followed by min-max normalise, not spatial slerp. bleh kept the same formula but renamed it bislerp_wrong.

entries.name: Probabilistic, gradient and slice blends
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Blends that pick values rather than mix them. Prob modes jitter t with noise or pick per element. Gradient makes a triangular ratio ramp across the flattened tensor or one dim. Slice modes rank or cut along a dim. Stochastic modes draw from torch's global RNG, so they depend on seed state rather than a widget.

entries.name: Progressive stage upscale with flow renoise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Multi-stage hires for flow models. Each stage resizes, then adds noise along the flow interpolation, which is a lerp between latent and noise, not additive sigma noise. Then a sampler pass; optional dilated stage blended by the FFT entry above. Sizes align to multiples of 2.

entries.name: Quantile normalise (percentile threshold family)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A percentile threshold per sample or globally, then one of many strategies: clamp, tanh, sigmoid, wave functions, scale down. Exposed as a latent operation, so it can run on the guidance delta through a CFG hook. This is the closest pack-side form of dynamic thresholding for latents in this scan; proper dynamic thresholding nodes sit in the guidance family.

entries.name: Radial band split on an unshifted FFT (bands swapped)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two nodes build a radial mask centred at (h/2, w/2) and multiply it onto an FFT that was never fftshift-ed. In an unshifted FFT, DC sits at the corner and the centre holds the highest frequencies. So the output labelled low or macro holds the highest frequencies and DC lands in the high or micro band. Recombining all bands still looks fine, which hides this.

entries.name: Rank-based distribution match and force-Gaussian
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Stronger than moment matching: replaces source values with reference values by rank, so the whole histogram transfers. Force-Gaussian maps ranks through the inverse error function so the result is exactly normal-shaped whatever came in. Robust scale uses median absolute deviation, so outliers do not set the scale.

entries.name: RES4LYF latent tools (short pointer)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: RES4LYF includes latent channel matching, channel normalise and offset, phase and magnitude offsets, and cosine-similarity slerp ratio search, with process_latent_in conversion to float64 in some paths. See the RES4LYF tribute page for details; not reproduced here.

entries.name: ReSharpen: sample delta boost via preview callback
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds or subtracts a tenth of 'details' times each step's change in x during sampling, to change detail: positive details subtract. It works by replacing latent_preview.prepare_callback globally at import time and editing x in place inside the callback. So the method is tied to samplers passing the live x to the callback.

entries.name: SD-Latent-Upscaler (conv net per scale)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Plain conv stack with nearest upsample after the first layer, trained per SD version and per scale. Weights are pulled from Hugging Face when absent. Input and output stay 4 channels.

entries.name: SesquiLSR (learned 1x to 2x, multi-format)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Learned arbitrary-scale upscaler with format adaptors, so packed or BN-normalised latents are converted to the raw VAE layout first, upscaled, then converted back. Adaptor maths runs in fp32 and the model at selected precision.

entries.name: Slerp per pixel across channels
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Each pixel's channel vector gets its own angle, the same axis bislerp uses, but with no magnitude lerp afterward. Different pixels rotate by different amounts. Catalogued as a short entry; see the RES4LYF tribute page.

entries.name: Slerp treating the entire batch as one vector
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Some nodes flatten across the batch too, so every sample in a batch shares one angle. With batch 1 this matches the per-sample form; with larger batches samples influence each other's interpolation.

entries.name: Slerp, one angle per batch sample
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: The classic latent slerp. Each sample is flattened to a single long vector, one angle is computed for it, and the raw (not unit) endpoints are mixed with sine weights. For near-orthogonal, equal-norm latents such as Gaussian noise the norm stays about constant, which is why it is used in place of lerp for noise. Norm is not explicitly restored when the two inputs differ in length.

entries.name: Soft-gated high frequency enhancer
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Separates low frequency with a Gaussian in shifted FFT space, then boosts high frequency only where its smoothed magnitude clears a threshold through a sigmoid. Keeps detail while avoiding noise amplification. A companion runs this between sampling steps.

entries.name: Spatial Gaussian frequency split and merge
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits by Gaussian blur, not FFT: low = blur, high = latent − low. Merging with gain 1 reconstructs exactly, and gains shift the balance. No periodicity assumption, so no wrap-around at edges. 5D goes through a per-frame reshape.

entries.name: Spectral band gain and progress-weighted trust
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Band masks are built correctly from fftfreq. One function boosts mid and attenuates highest frequencies. Another reweights denoised output by progress, trusting highs less early. The "quantum" in the pack name is branding; this part is FFT gains with a golden-ratio exponent.

entries.name: Spectral power-law shaping and phase scramble
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: SpectralShape tilts the whole spectrum by a power of radial frequency, optionally restoring energy. PhaseScramble randomises phase by a seeded amount along the shortest arc while keeping magnitude, which destroys structure and keeps texture stats. The radius and decompose helpers live in the missing core/freq.py, so only the node-level maths is confirmed.

entries.name: Temporal gradient blend over batch
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Crossfades two equal-length latent batches by batch index, for video-as-batch transitions. No variance correction, so the middle of the fade loses variance. It writes into samples_out["samples"], the shallow-copied samples1 tensor.

entries.name: Tile blend with raised-cosine ramps
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Alternative to core's linear feather. Complementary raised-cosine ramps sum to 1 exactly across an overlap band, so a constant signal stays constant even before division. Radiance avoids zero weight by offsetting the ramp.

entries.name: Tonemap on channel 0 only (Reinhard, Möbius, ACES-like)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same white-point recipe as core but applied only to channel 0, treated as luminance, with a choice of three curves. On a one-channel slice the vector norm is just |x|, so the sign is kept and the magnitude is compressed. Treating channel 0 as luminance is the pack's assumption.

entries.name: Unsharp sharpen in latent
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: High pass from an OpenCV blur, scaled. Factor 1 is identity, above 1 sharpens, and negative inverts detail. Simple and shape-preserving.

entries.name: Variance-aware blends: pythagorean lerp, orbit, RMS, cosine, cubic
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: bleh has blends that handle variance loss on purpose. Pythagorean lerp rescales weights so squares sum to 1 at the default, the right correction for independent inputs. Orbit moves on a quarter circle so endpoints are a and b. RMS interpolates in a power domain. Cosine and cubic only reshape t and do not correct variance.

entries.name: WAS BlendLatents, output rescaled to 0..1
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Twelve image-style modes on latents, and the result of every mode is min-max rescaled to 0..1 over the whole tensor. That removes negative values and the original scale of the latent, so downstream sampling sees a very different distribution. The docstring states the rescale, so it is intended.

entries.name: Wavelet blend (DWT sub-bands)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Decomposes a and b with a wavelet transform, blends low and high sub-bands with separately chosen modes and factors, and inverts. Optional sub-band offsets per level. The FIXME comments flag doubts about 5D reshaping, and a debug print fires on each call.

entries.name: Whiten, resize, recolour upscale
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Removes channel correlations with an eigendecomposition of the channel covariance, resizes in decorrelated space, recolours, and can match moments again. Statistics can come from another latent. Unusually rigorous about variance across channels.

entries.name: Z-score and related scale normalisers
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Plain rescales to unit variance, differing in scope, and scope matters most. SV uses a single global mean/std across the batch and channels, so samples bleed into one another. CampB does per sample. Valkymaera offers a list and a per_channel switch (list read, bodies not). JTrigger can keep the mean.

entries.name: À trous wavelet colour fix (image space)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Image-space. Dilated 3×3 blurs at radii 1..16 give a high band and a low band, and output combines high frequencies of the content with low frequencies of the reference. Common after upscalers and SeedVR2. These operate on IMAGE not LATENT, listed since their names surface in the latent function digest.

entries.name: μ-centred slerp
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Slerp around a population centroid rather than the origin. It subtracts μ, slerps directions, lerps the radius, adds μ back. Useful when the latent has a non-zero mean, because origin-centred slerp then bends through a different arc. When μ is not given, the function uses per-channel mean over batch and space.

entries.name: ComfyMathExpression (simpleeval)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Core scalar expression node. It runs user text through the simpleeval library with a fixed function table, against named numeric inputs a..z, and returns float, int and bool. Not Python eval; pow is wrapped with an exponent cap. Tensors are not accepted.

entries.name: Core boolean and switch nodes
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Generic flow utilities. Not, And and Or use Python truthiness; Switch and Soft Switch pick an input lazily, so the unused branch is not evaluated. Soft Switch tolerates one input being unconnected.

entries.name: simpleeval-based evaluators
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Same library core uses. Each call passes a fixed set of names, and the library does the parsing. Lower risk than eval by repute; the library itself was not reviewed here.

entries.name: AST-walking calculators (no eval)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Parse with Python ast or their own grammar and only permit known node types and functions. These are the safest of the custom expression nodes. The AusBoss description states shared workflows cannot smuggle code. CyWP does this for tensors.

entries.name: Boolean and compare nodes in packs
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Very many packs add number compare, logic gates, and branch nodes. They mostly differ in naming and laziness. ComfyMath separates unary and binary boolean ops. Impact's compare is a plain node, and its separate conditional branch node has the lazy inputs. No sampling maths; not enumerated individually.

entries.name: Curve and easing maths
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Remap a value through a named or written curve, usually for schedules. WAS maps a list through named easings between ranges. SV parses curves with a regex-based interpreter, with no eval. AKatz takes a Python expression through builtins-free eval. Sigma-curve editors (NKD Sigmas Curve, Olm CurveEditor, ComfyUI_Curves, by name only) are the graphical relatives.

entries.name: numexpr and sympy based expressions
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Keyframe-curve and sigma-function nodes use a numeric or symbolic library. FizzNodes uses numexpr for value schedules, Hangover-Utils uses sympy parsers. sympy parse_expr is believed to use eval internally, which was not checked here (see the inference claim).

entries.name: RISK: blocklist or character-filter guarded eval
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Eval after screening text. A strict digit-and-operator regex (Utilitools) is workable since names cannot appear. A keyword blocklist (WJNodes) is weaker, since blocklists are usually incomplete. WJNodes evaluates on tensors, so this is also image math.

entries.name: RISK: eval with builtins removed
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Python eval with __builtins__ emptied and a table of allowed functions. The common calculator pattern. Keeps honest use simple but is not a sandbox: Python attribute access stays available unless blocked, so treat as weaker than a real parser. RES4LYF adds numpy's whole namespace to its one. DebugPadawan's comment acknowledges the trade-off.

entries.name: RISK: raw Python eval/exec of a text widget
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: These nodes run widget text as Python with normal builtins available, or no sandbox at all. A shared workflow is then able to run arbitrary code on this box as soon as it is queued. Treat a workflow using them as code. Not a maths method so much as a hazard to note on each provider.

entries.name: Statistics and inspection
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Report tensor statistics or compute them for a data flow. Mostly pass-through debug nodes, plus a large data-analysis pack that wraps standard libraries. Useful pre-flight when using the normalisers above, since many outputs depend on scope.

entries.name: Tensor math expression nodes
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Expression over whole tensors rather than scalars. CyWP TorchSymbolic has its own parser with a torch function table, no Python eval. TEX is a compiled per-pixel language that generates Python and execs it, so safety rests on its compiler. Eden and WJNodes eval over tensors. more_math is the widest in scope by its node list (Latent, Noise, Model, VAE, CLIP, Audio), but its source is not on disk, so it is listed from node names only.

entries.name: Attention Multiply (q/k/v/out weight scale)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales the projection weights of attention layers instead of the attention values at runtime. It is a weight patch, like a LoRA with no delta, so it triggers a weight change on load.

entries.name: Block-Sparse Attention (Sol-Attn / SLA / VSA)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Replaces dense self-attention with a block-sparse kernel from comfy_kitchen, where each query block attends exactly to a chosen subset of key blocks. Three selection modes: an adaptive per-head threshold (sol-attn), a fixed top percent (sla), and 3D video-cube tiling with a learned coarse branch (vsa). Falls back to the dense backend outside the sigma window, under the token minimum, on listed blocks, or when dtype/head_dim/device don't fit.

entries.name: Context windows (latent frame windowing)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs the model over overlapping frame windows and fuses, so a video model can sample more frames than its context. Each step makes as many model calls as windows. Core offers flat, pyramid and overlap-linear weights, plus relative for static schedules, with several window schedules.

entries.name: Core ModelPatcher patch API (reference)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A reference entry for the hooks that other entries cite. Most hacks reach the model through these rather than editing it. Each call is cloned per node, so patches stay local to one MODEL wire unless a pack bypasses this.

entries.name: Differential Diffusion (soft mask)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Lets a greyscale mask act as a per-pixel denoise strength. At each step only pixels whose mask value exceeds a falling threshold can change, so regions join the edit at different times. Core adds a strength blend back to the soft mask.

entries.name: EasyCache
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Skips whole model forwards when predicted output change is small, then adds the cached output−input difference to the current input. It estimates output change from the measured input change and the last-seen ratio of output change to input change. Needs no per-model calibration, unlike TeaCache.

entries.name: Flux KV Cache (reference tokens)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Caches reference image K and V from the first pass so later steps skip those tokens in the input. Saves work for edit models whose reference image doesn't change, on the assumption the reference's features are close to fixed.

entries.name: FreeU (v1)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Rescales UNet decoder features before they merge with the encoder skip: the first half of the backbone channels gets a flat gain, and the skip's low frequencies are attenuated in FFT space. Used to shift the balance between backbone denoising and skip detail on SD-style UNets.

entries.name: FreeU V2
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: FreeU with a structure-aware backbone gain: the gain is strongest where the channel-mean feature map is brightest, instead of flat. The skip filter is the same as v1. The node also has higher defaults for the b values.

entries.name: H3 PDD output-head bank fusion
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A distilled H3 LoRA can carry several stacked output heads, one per fine training step. An actual sampler step spans several fine steps, so the output head used on that step is a dt-weighted mix of those heads. Core handles a converted bank natively; several packs instead load the official files and fuse the heads themselves, and they differ on what the stored heads mean and on which schedules they allow.

entries.name: HiDream-O1 Patch Seam Smoothing
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs the model extra times on circularly shifted inputs and blends the unshifted predictions to hide the 32-pixel patch grid. Costs one extra model call per extra shift, inside a percent window. Edge rows are feathered back to the unshifted prediction to hide wraparound.

entries.name: HyperTile
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits self-attention query tokens into a grid of tiles to cut attention cost at high resolution. At the default swap_size of 2 the grid is fixed, because the last candidate can never be drawn; it only varies per call with swap_size 3 or more and enough divisors. Only the query is rearranged by this patch; keys and values are passed back untouched.

entries.name: Kohya Deep Shrink (PatchModelAddDownscale)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Downscales the UNet feature map at one input block during early sampling, then upsizes on the decoder side to match the skip. This keeps early composition at training resolution when generating larger images, avoiding repeated subjects.

entries.name: LazyCache
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A simplified EasyCache wrapped around predict_noise instead of the diffusion model, so it caches the guided result rather than each cond. Its description says it works worse overall but is universal. There is one cache_diff, not one per cond.

entries.name: Model Attention Backend / Compute Dtype
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Per-model choice of the dense attention function (PyTorch or Comfy Kitchen int8), and a separate node that forces compute dtype. The dtype path regenerates the patch uuid, so it forces a full reload.

entries.name: ModelNoiseScale
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sets a noise multiplier on flow models whose training used noise larger than unit variance. It keeps shift and multiplier and only rebuilds the sampling object.

entries.name: ModelSampling prediction-type overrides
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: These nodes swap the model's sampling object, telling the sampler how to read model output. Shift values are covered by the scheduler pages; this entry records the prediction maths. Using the wrong type gives broken results, since x0 is computed differently in each one.

entries.name: RenormCFG (Lumina2)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A replacement CFG function that does classic CFG only below a limit compared with sigma (the args key is named timestep but holds sigma), and caps the guided output's norm at a multiple of the conditional's norm. Above the limit it just returns the conditional. It only operates on the first in_channels; other channels pass through from cond.

entries.name: RoPE options (scale/shift)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales and shifts rotary position coordinates, to change spatial and temporal alignment across the frame without changing the weights. RifleX and untwisting variants act on this area.

entries.name: SageAttention selection and H3/Wan memory-efficient patches
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Routes attention through the SageAttention quantized kernel, per model or globally. Same attention maths with less exactness; many nodes exist because old cards, AMD or head dims fail in differing ways. Core selects at startup by flag; nodes do it per-model through the override; a few do it globally.

entries.name: Sequential vs batched CFG
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Whether cond and uncond are run in one batch or one after the other. Core decides this itself by memory, so no flag exists in stock KSampler: it fits as many as free memory allows. Video wrappers expose an explicit batched_cfg bool and default to sequential, saving memory for a slower step.

entries.name: Temporal Score Rescaling (TSR)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Post-CFG rescale of the score that steers output diversity by a signal-to-noise dependent ratio. The node text says lower k gives more detail and higher k gives smoother results; k=1 turns it off.

entries.name: ToMe (Token Merging, tomesd port)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Merges similar self-attention query tokens before attention and restores them after, so fewer queries run. Speeds up sampling at some detail cost. Only runs on the highest-resolution attention blocks, and the core port leaves keys and values at full length.

entries.name: WanAnimate2Cache (pose branch cache)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs the Animate 2 pose branch once and reuses its block inputs across all later sampling steps instead of recomputing, since pose doesn't change with sampling step. The node's own text says about half the generation time at a cost of about 12.5 GB of RAM at 480×832/81 frames in bf16.

entries.name: Attention Couple (region prompts by masked cross-attention)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs cross-attention once per region prompt and combines outputs using spatial masks normalised to sum to 1, so different prompts rule different areas. Original replaces attn2; later forks use attn2_patch to expand the batch, which keeps other hooks working. Unlike latent couple, there is one model call but several attention calls in each block.

entries.name: Attention temperature
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Changes the softmax sharpness of self or cross attention, with options to tune it from resolution or token variance. Higher temperature flattens attention. Extraltodeus's node replaces attention by block.

entries.name: Block CFG and block ops
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Applies a guidance-like push between cond and uncond at chosen UNet blocks, in feature space instead of the output. Block ops let one write conditional scripts of operations such as scale, flip and FFT on block features.

entries.name: Cache Accelerator: fixed-interval x0 extrapolation (Wtl)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs the model on a fixed rhythm inside a step window and predicts the x0 of the skipped evaluations from the last three real ones. It has no change threshold, so the speedup is set in advance. The prediction shrinks towards holding x0 when the recent motion reversed, and it keeps fine detail from a plain linear guess while taking coarse structure from the careful one.

entries.name: CacheDiT (DBCache + TaylorSeer adapter, and fixed-interval fallback)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Wraps the external cache_dit library's block adapter, which reuses middle blocks with first and last blocks computed. Where the adapter isn't used, a built-in fallback replaces transformer.forward with a simple rule that returns the last whole output on every Nth call, optionally plus random noise.

entries.name: CachedSearch: best-of-N seeds on cached drafts
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Uses a step cache to make seed search cheap instead of to make the final render fast. Every candidate seed is sampled with core EasyCache, decoded and scored by an image-reward model, then the winning seed is sampled again with the cache off. Sampling is seeded, so the delivered latent is a plain full-compute render of that seed.

entries.name: CADS (cond annealed by noise)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds noise to text conditioning early in sampling, decaying through a window, to widen variety, then renormalises to keep the original stats. Implemented at the cond-batch level so every model call gets it.

entries.name: Chroma Cache (FBCache skeleton, shape-only check)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A Chroma-only cache adapted from FBCache code, where the similarity check has been reduced to a shape comparison and the threshold input commented out. In effect a pure percent window and interval decide reuse.

entries.name: DeepCache
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: On most steps it runs only the shallow UNet blocks and reuses the deep decoder feature from the last full step. Interval-based, with no change metric at all. The wrapper reimplements the UNet forward, so it can miss hooks added to core since.

entries.name: DenseDiffusion (attention mask regulation)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Reweights the cross-attention score map before softmax so tokens in each regional prompt are favoured inside their mask. Uses a custom attention path replacing attn2 across blocks.

entries.name: DiT block skipping (speed)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Skips listed transformer blocks entirely, on every step, for speed. Not guidance: it is a plain omission with no compensation, so quality depends on which blocks.

entries.name: Fast terminate per block
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Checks for user interrupt at each block rather than per step, so cancel on large models responds sooner. A pure ops hack with no effect on output.

entries.name: FETA / Enhance-A-Video
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Boosts self-attention output by a score derived from temporal attention dispersion, intended to sharpen video. Per step scaling comes from how flat the frame-to-frame attention is.

entries.name: First Block Cache (FBCache)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs the first transformer block every step, and compares its output or residual to the previous step's. If they barely changed, the remaining blocks are skipped and a stored tail residual is applied. It uses a real model output as the signal, so needs no per-model calibration, at the cost of one block per step.

entries.name: Fooocus inpaint head patch
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds a learned inpaint head's feature to the first input block, plus a LoRA-style weight patch. The head reads mask and latent. It's the standard way these packs bring Fooocus inpaint to Comfy.

entries.name: FreeU advanced forks
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Forks that widen FreeU: a sigma window, slices by channel count, blending modes for the backbone gain, multi-scale Fourier masks, a choice of target blocks. Sonar's FreeU Extreme replaces the Fourier box with a configurable power filter by stage.

entries.name: Global torch/comfy monkey patches (risk register)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Not a method but a warning list. These packs replace functions on torch or comfy for the whole process, usually when a node runs or even at import, instead of using the patch API on one MODEL wire. If one breaks or never restores, every later job is affected. Listed from static grep; a pack needs to be installed and sometimes run for each to take effect.

entries.name: Gradient and scripted Deep Shrink
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Deep Shrink with a downscale factor that varies through sampling, by a percentage table with optional interpolation, rather than a fixed factor in a window. Other forks add multiple blocks and a fade-out. bleh's variant fades its scale out toward the end of its window.

entries.name: H3 activation-space LoRA with int8 fc2 routing
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Applies a small low-rank update at run time, by adding it to a layer's output, instead of merging it into weights where quantization would round it away. It adds in place to save peak memory. MLP fc2 layers on int8 bases must still be merged, because core's fused kernel reads the weight directly and a forward hook on them never fires.

entries.name: H3 AdaLN trajectory precompute (Sol-H3 helper)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Computes every block's large AdaLN projection once for the whole sampling schedule, then swaps those modules for parameter-free lookups, so the big weights need not stay loaded during denoising. An unknown timestep table falls back to the original module. This is an exact cache of a deterministic function, not an approximation.

entries.name: H3 Adaptive Tail Cache
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A MiniMax H3 cache that always computes leading blocks and may skip the trailing portion, using sigma gap, a consecutive limit, and a content score from the warm-prefix output. The content limit adapts by an EMA of earlier scores. It also manages residuals on CPU or GPU with a safety margin.

entries.name: H3 Diff-Aid-style text row gain
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Scales only the text rows of H3's packed sequence just before chosen blocks, which raises or lowers text features in those blocks. It has no trained weights, unlike the Diff-Aid idea it adapts. The node's own text says no quality gain has been established.

entries.name: H3 MLP sequence chunking
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs each H3 block's MLP over slices of the token sequence and joins the results, to cut peak activation memory. The MLP works token by token, so the docstring argues the result is the same as the unchunked call. It only chunks sequences long enough to matter.

entries.name: H3 MotionCache
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An EasyCache-style predictor for H3 that weights video change by where frames differ most, and also watches audio. It predicts output change from input change and skips when the accumulated estimate stays low.

entries.name: H3 multi-probe Block Cache (T8)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A MiniMax H3 cache that measures change after several probe blocks and compares global, audio and video indicators, with separate tails for audio and video. It stops the model through an exception once it decides to hit. Only the global score gates, in the code read.

entries.name: H3 native temporal alignment (TARA)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Lines up a reference video's clock with the output's clock, then softly discourages output tokens from attending to reference motion tokens far away in time. It is meant to run with a matching motion-transfer LoRA. The node requires identical temporal grids and refuses to stretch motion to fit.

entries.name: H3 pruned-base AdaLN LoRA reinjection
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Pruned H3 checkpoints replace the time embedder with a small curve table, so a LoRA's AdaLN update has no matching weight to patch. Two routes were found. One recovers the missing embedding at run time from a bundled grid and adds the update to each projection's output. The other refits the update into the pruned curve space by least squares, once, and rejects a poor fit.

entries.name: H3 PTD per-step adapters (WAS)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Applies a Parametric Trajectory Distillation file so H3 samples in 4 to 8 steps. Instead of one LoRA, each sampler step gets its own low-rank updates, added at run time to the layer outputs, and on Ref2VA files its own head pair. The node also outputs the sigmas the file was trained at, and sampling on other sigmas raises an error.

entries.name: H3 whole block-stack residual cache (DaSiWa)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Skips all H3 transformer blocks at once on some steps and adds the block stack's last residual to the current input instead. The decision compares a thin sample of the stack's input between steps, so no block has to run to decide. It needs a replaced model forward, because core has no patch point around the whole block loop.

entries.name: HiCache / HiCache++
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Feature forecast with scaled Hermite polynomials instead of Taylor, or a dynamic mode decomposition basis in the ++ form. The Archerkattri packs use it for 3D shape pipelines rather than the sampler model API, replacing pipeline.model with a wrapper module.

entries.name: HiDiffusion MSW-MSA attention
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Multi-scale shifted-window self-attention from HiDiffusion. Tokens are split into 2×2 windows with a shift that changes between blocks, to cut attention cost at high resolution. It reworks the attention batch rather than the model.

entries.name: HiDiffusion RAU-Net
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Resolution-aware UNet hack: during early sampling, replaces a chosen downsample conv with a dilated stride-4 version and upsamples by matching interpolation, and also scales features at chosen cross-attention blocks. The goal is keeping composition stable at high resolution, like Deep Shrink, but by altering the sampling ops. Controlled by presets for SD1.5 and SDXL.

entries.name: HyperFlow two-time (t, r) conditioning
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Conditions each H3 denoising step on the interval it integrates rather than on one time point. The port swaps the time embedder for a mix of the normal embedding of t and a second embedding of the step's endpoint r, built from raw weights plus a LoRA. Rows are remapped per stream, because video and audio have different endpoints.

entries.name: LoRA Block Weight
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Applies a LoRA with a per-block strength vector, to take e.g. only style or composition. This is a weight patch at load, so it costs nothing per step, but acts as a static change.

entries.name: LoRTnoC input hint
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A LoRA for ControlNet-like control, with a hint encoder added to the first input block's features.

entries.name: MagCache (magnitude-ratio cache)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Skips based on a precomputed table of how the residual's magnitude changes step to step, rather than on the live input. Error accumulates as the running ratio drifts from 1, with a hard cap on consecutive skips and an initial retention window. Needs a ratio table for the model, or a calibration run.

entries.name: MeanCache
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: On skipped steps it uses an estimate of the average velocity over the interval, built from a finite difference of past velocities, instead of repeating the last velocity. With PSSP on (the default) a precomputed skip schedule decides, and a peak limit and accumulated error can veto a skip. The relative threshold gate is used only with PSSP off. Presets are named by quality in the node.

entries.name: NABLA sparse attention (KJ)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An experimental sparse attention for video where a block mask comes from a static window mask plus a thresholded similarity, applied at the attention override.

entries.name: Negative attention
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds a term to the positive prompt's attention scores from the difference between positive and negative attention outputs. It expects a cond tokens doubled by concat.

entries.name: NegPiP (negative prompt inside positive)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Lets a negative token weight flip only the value vector in cross-attention, not the key, so the token subtracts where it would attend. The CLIP encoder is hooked to encode key and value alternately, and the patch splits them back.

entries.name: Prompt Injection (per-block cond)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Replaces cross-attention context at specified blocks with another conditioning, so a block group gets a different prompt, within a sigma window. This builds a tensor with the first cond plus the injected cond multiplied by weight.

entries.name: Pruna cache nodes
entries.label: inference
entries.plain: Thin ComfyUI wrappers around the external pruna or pruna_pro package's smash() caching. Modes and logic are in the external package and aren't readable here. Offers adaptive, periodic and auto policies, with taylor, ab and bdf modes named.

entries.name: Radial attention (sparse by frame distance)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Sparse temporal self-attention where each token attends to nearby frames densely, and to far frames in narrow windows that shrink with distance, plus occasional full far frames. Early dense steps are kept. The mask builds per sequence and runs through a block-sparse Sage kernel.

entries.name: Reference-only / shared self-attention
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs the reference image's latent in the same batch and appends its queries to other batch items' keys, so they draw on its features. Style-aligned forks do the same across a batch with different normalisation.

entries.name: Regional joint-attention boolean mask (HunyuanLoom)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds each region's prompt tokens to the context and builds one boolean mask over text and video tokens. Each region's text can only see its own tokens and its own area, and tokens in different regions cannot see each other unless they are background. It works by hard masking, not by reweighting.

entries.name: Regional log-coverage cross-attention bias (bv)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Concatenates all regional prompts into one context and adds a per-token logit bias to cross-attention, based on how much of each query token a region covers. Uncovered pairs get minus infinity. Outside the active sigma window the bias stays in force with strength zero, so the regional prompts stay hidden rather than becoming global.

entries.name: Regional LoRA by masked activation (Nougan)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Gives two characters separate LoRAs on one model, by adding each LoRA's output delta only on the tokens inside its soft rectangle. The rectangle is built on the token grid with sigmoid edges and text tokens get zero. Prompts are separately attached with ordinary conditioning masks.

entries.name: Regional LoRA by masked hook conditioning (RS)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits conditioning into copies, one per LoRA group, each masked to that character's area with core's hook system, so a pass runs per group in precision mode. Overlaps are normalised and box regions take priority over point regions. A shared normal mode exists and is tried first when selected.

entries.name: Regional tracked map with logit routing (Nynxz)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Keeps a region map that can move with the content during sampling, by reclustering canvas key features at a few middle blocks. It sends each canvas token to its region's own copy of the prompt with a logit bias. Mixing by log weight means that identical copies read as the one prompt. An optional isolation bias also pushes regions apart, and the code's notes warn it costs shared lighting.

entries.name: Sampler-level step skips (AdaptiveDiff, SADA, ZEUS, sampler EasyCache)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: AccelDiff also replaces k-diffusion sampler loops with versions that skip model calls based on the output's trend. These live in the sampler rather than a model patch, so they can skip every cond at once. AdaptiveDiff checks second-difference smoothness, SADA uses a momentum sign and Lagrange interpolation, and ZEUS uses a fixed modular skip pattern.

entries.name: ScaleCrafter (conv dilation)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Enlarges UNet convolution receptive fields at high resolution by dilating 3×3 convolutions inside a timestep range, with bicubic resampling of input when the rate isn't an integer. This also targets repeated subjects at larger than training size.

entries.name: SeaCache
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: TeaCache-like accumulation, but the change metric is computed after a sigma-dependent spectral filter, so frequency bands the current noise level hides don't count. No polynomial calibration is needed in this pack. H3 gets a separate runtime with video and audio accumulators.

entries.name: Seamless tiling (circular conv padding)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Makes image borders wrap so output tiles seamlessly by altering every Conv2d's padding to be circular on the chosen axes. The DiT variant instead rolls the latent by a per-step offset during sampling, and makes the VAE decoder circular.

entries.name: Spectrum (Chebyshev feature forecasting)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fits a Chebyshev-basis ridge regression through past outputs or features over time, and predicts them on cached steps, blended with a first-order extrapolation. Real steps get sparser as a flexible window grows. Implementations disagree on what is forecast: whole denoised output, or the feature just before the final layer.

entries.name: SpotEdit (region reuse in edit models)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: For Qwen edit models: tokens outside an edit mask reuse a cached result and only masked tokens run blocks, from a difference mask between original and modified latents.

entries.name: T-GATE (cached attention after a gate)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: After a sigma gate, it stops computing cross-attention, and optionally self-attention, reusing the last computed batch's cached result, averaged over cond and uncond once CFG is off. Past the gate the uncond pass is dropped and cfg becomes 1. This saves the attention calls while still running conv blocks. It replaces the transformer block forward.

entries.name: TaylorSeer
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Instead of reusing old features, it forecasts them with a Taylor series built from finite differences at earlier computed steps, per block and module. Steps alternate between full computation every N steps and forecasted ones. Memory grows with block count unless the Lite node is used, which forecasts one tensor.

entries.name: TC-Padé residual predictor
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Predicts the whole transformer stack's residual from recent residuals using a rational (Padé-like) formula with a per-element stability factor. Predicts on all non-interval steps inside a range, regardless of how much the signal changed.

entries.name: TeaCache (timestep-embedding-aware cache)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Skips the DiT block stack when the first block's modulated input has hardly changed since the last computed step, and re-adds the stored residual instead. The raw relative change is mapped through a per-model polynomial, then accumulated until it crosses the threshold. Polynomial coefficients are per architecture and per Wan variant, so the model_type must match.

entries.name: Tiled Diffusion (MultiDiffusion, SpotDiffusion)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Splits the latent into tiles per step and calls the model per tile, then blends, to allow large images within memory. SpotDiffusion randomly rolls the latent each step so tile seams land in a new place and needs no overlap.

entries.name: TurboTeaCache (TeaCache with quantized residuals)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A TeaCache variant that stores residuals through a vector-quantizer buffer to save memory, and optionally extrapolates from the two most recent residuals. The pack's Wan 2.2 coefficient is a stated proxy for 2.1.

entries.name: TwinFlow (few-step with target-time embedder)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A few-step method where the model also knows the target timestep through a second time embedder. The pack loads extra embedder weights onto native Z-Image or Qwen-Image models and adds its own sampler. It needs a TwinFlow checkpoint.

entries.name: OCS sampler groups (switch method by step, percent or sigma)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: One OCS Sampler holds a chain of groups. Each group says when it applies, by step number, share of the steps or sigma, and which step methods it runs. At every step the first group whose window matches does the work, so euler can run the first few steps and dpmpp_sde the rest inside one sampler.

entries.name: OCS substep merge strategies
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A group can run several substeps per step, from one or more methods, and a merge strategy decides how they combine. simple runs one; supreme_avg averages the substep results and renoises; divide splits the step into smaller sigma steps; overshoot steps past the target and comes back with Restart-style noise; lookahead and pingpong run ahead on a copy and keep part of what they learn.

entries.name: OCS ports of core samplers
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: OCS carries its own copies of euler, dpmpp_2m, dpmpp_2m_sde, dpmpp_3m_sde, dpmpp_2s, dpmpp_sde, ipndm, ipndm_v, deis, gradient_estimation, heunpp2, dpm_2 and res_multistep, based on ComfyUI's versions. They exist so the groups and merge strategies above can schedule them; on their own they aim to match core.

entries.name: Reversible Heun (and its one-call history form)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A Heun step written as a blend: it predicts at the lower sigma, blends the two clean-image guesses with a weight set by the sigma ratio, and can subtract a reversible correction built from the change in slope. The 1s form reuses the previous step's prediction instead of a new call when it can.

entries.name: RES (second-order exponential step)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A two-stage exponential integrator in log-sigma time: one extra model call at the midpoint, with phi-function weights for the two clean-image guesses. It is the same family as RES4LYF's res_2s, in Clybius's version.

entries.name: Runge-Kutta steps: Bogacki-Shampine, RK4, RKF45, dynamic RK
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Classic Runge-Kutta steps applied to the sigma ODE. Bogacki-Shampine uses three slopes (two extra calls) and can add a reversible correction; RK4 uses four; rkf45 uses the six Fehlberg stages but keeps only the fourth-order answer, with no step-size control; rk_dynamic picks its order from how much the prediction changed since the last step.

entries.name: Euler Dancing
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: An ancestral Euler step that aims further down the schedule than the next sigma (two steps by default), adds the noise for that leap, then steps back up toward the real next sigma. The current code prints debug lines to the console on every step.

entries.name: TTM-JVP (second-order Taylor step with a Jacobian-vector product)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: A truncated Taylor step that asks the model not just for its clean-image guess but for how that guess changes along the step, using a forward-mode derivative through the model. That costs one extra pass with tangents, and more memory than a plain call.

entries.name: SENS (DPM++ 2M SDE with reversible terms)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: DPM++ 2M SDE with up to two extra reversible correction terms built from the previous one and two predictions. With the corrections at zero it is DPM++ 2M SDE.

entries.name: Distance sampler
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Each step tries several Euler moves (three by default, falling to one near the end), asks the model at the next sigma for each, and blends the slopes with weights that favour the ones closest to the rest. It spends extra model calls to steady the step.

entries.name: Ping-pong step
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Inside its window the step jumps straight to the model's clean-image guess and renoises to the next sigma with fresh noise; outside it, plain Euler. Its default window is step 0 only, so it acts like Euler unless the window is widened.

entries.name: Cycle steps (euler and trapezoidal)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: blepping's own steps that keep part of the predicted noise and replace the rest with fresh noise at every step, by a fixed share (cycle_pct, 0.25 by default). The trapezoidal form makes one extra call at the next sigma and blends the two guesses first.

entries.name: Batch-augmented and wavelet steps (blep_bas, blep_weoon)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Two experiments of blepping's. blep_bas runs the model on a larger batch built from the latent for its first few steps (0 to 3 by default) and folds the results back. blep_weoon splits the step in wavelet bands and blends them separately; it needs pytorch_wavelets.

entries.name: ODE and SDE library backends (torchdiffeq, torchsde, torchode, diffrax)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Hands each step to an outside solver library, which picks its own internal steps. tde uses torchdiffeq, tsde torchsde, tode torchode and diffrax the JAX library. Each is optional and only offered when its library is installed. The README advises against SDE mode for now.

entries.name: OCS Restart schedule
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Builds a Restart-sampling sigma list from an ordinary schedule and a short text rule, such as 'every 5 steps, jump back 3'. The OCS Sampler sees each jump back up and adds the matching noise. With an empty rule it returns the schedule unchanged.

entries.name: Immiscible noise (assign noise to the latent it is closest to)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Draws a batch of candidate noises and keeps, for each slice of the latent (by channel by default), the candidate nearest a reference such as the positive prediction. The idea comes from a 2024 paper on training; the README notes it was made for training, not sampling.

entries.name: OCS Perlin noise
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Fractal Perlin noise at latent size, with octaves, persistence and lacunarity, and a break_pattern setting that mixes it with ordinary noise. It can be handed to Sonar's noise inputs through a converter node.

entries.name: OCS expression language and filters
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Parameters and filters can be written as small expressions in OCS's own language, read by its own parser, not by Python. Calls into torch are off unless an environment variable allows them; with them off, a workflow's expressions can only use the built-in functions.

entries.name: Set a model's maximum sigma
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Gives a copy of the model a different top sigma, by scaling its sigma table, so a scheduler fed from it starts higher or lower. Meant for the scheduler, not the sampler.

entries.name: Mesh drag (warp a latent by dragging random mesh points)
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Picks random points on a coarse mesh over the latent, drags each a random distance, smooths the displacement with B-spline passes and resamples the latent through it. A seeded, local smear that keeps the latent's values but moves them.

entries.name: Fluid advection and smoke simulation on latents
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Runs a small fluid simulation over the latent: random forces stir a velocity field, which is damped, diffused and given vorticity, and the latent is carried along it step by step. The smoke version also carries a density field from a random source.

entries.name: Conditioning noise, blur, frequency split and scale
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Changes the text conditioning itself rather than the latent: adds seeded noise scaled by the embedding's own spread, blurs it along the token axis, splits it into smooth and detailed parts and merges them, or multiplies it by a factor. The pooled output is treated the same way where there is one.

entries.name: TurboQuant and RotorQuant attention
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Per-model attention patches that change the numbers attention sees, then call the normal attention. TurboQuant rotates queries and keys by a seeded orthogonal matrix and rounds the keys (and, if asked, the values) to a few bits on a normal-distribution codebook. RotorQuant rotates channels in groups of three and keeps some of each group. Both run ordinary attention on the result, so they model the error of compressed attention rather than saving memory or time; RotorQuant keeping all three components is a pure rotation and changes nothing but rounding.

entries.name: Seeded Gaussian noise for latents and images
entries.label: from code
entries.plain: Adds seeded Gaussian noise scaled by the tensor's own spread, so the same strength means the same relative change on any model's latent. Its image node is named ImageAddNoise, the same as a core node, so ComfyUI keeps core's node and drops this one.

coverage.static_scan: every .py file of every pack with source was parsed (AST only, never run)

surprises.text: The ddim sampler name gives the same pixels as euler (same seed, same graph). Core maps the name to Euler; only the inpaint noise option differs.
CFGNorm at strength 1 with CFG 14 washed an SDXL render to pale grey on this seed, while Rescale and APG at the same CFG stayed usable.

The linear_quadratic schedule with dpmpp_2m smeared an SDXL render at 20 steps, with rainbow speckle. On this model its last non-zero sigma at 20 steps is 2.67, against 0.03 for karras, so the last step jumps a long way to zero.
ddim_uniform starts lower than the rest: sigma 11.03 at 20 steps on SD and SDXL, where the others start at 14.61. It rendered brighter, with a different layout.
Karras at 20 steps broke SD 3.5 Medium with Euler (brown and unfinished), while simple, beta and kl_optimal held together on the same seed.
dpmpp_2s_ancestral_cfg_pp subtracts stage-2 uncond from stage-1 guided x0: the second model call overwrites temp[0] before the final update reads it, so the update uses D₁−U₂.

uni_pc replaces final σ=0 with 0.001 through a view (sigmas[:]), mutating sigmas. KSAMPLER then applies inverse_noise_scaling at 0.001, so on CONST models the result is divided by 0.999; sampling also stops at σ=0.001. One-step runs never move x (read, not run).

dpm_fast and dpm_adaptive throw away the schedule. Only sigmas[0], the last non-zero σ (and for dpm_fast the length) are used, sampling stops at sigmas[-2] with no denoise-to-zero, and sigmas [σ,0] give zero movement (read, not run).
SamplerEulerCFGpp version=alternative ends with 2D−U rather than D: the last step adds the guidance gap again. Regular version is different code.
cfgpp_ud10_ab does not return the model's last x0: at σ'=0 it replaces x with a linear extrapolation of D to σ=0 (zero_weight=1.0). It also keeps the cfg=1 shortcut, unlike other CFG++ samplers.

Flow-model handling is uneven. Only euler_ancestral, dpm_2_ancestral and dpmpp_2s_ancestral dispatch to RF code; res_multistep_ancestral and dpmpp_2s_ancestral_cfg_pp run VE ancestral maths on flow σ; dpmpp_2m uses −log σ while 2M SDE uses logit. The 2S RF path also sets its midpoint to 0.9999 at σ=1.0.
deis coefficients use fixed EDM constants (σ_min 0.002, σ_max 80), not the model's schedule, on every model including flow.

The ddim name runs Euler with different inpaint noise; an unknown sampler name given to KSampler silently becomes euler; KSampler alone discards the penultimate σ for dpm_2, dpm_2_ancestral, uni_pc and uni_pc_bh2, so a SamplerCustom graph gets a different schedule. The only literal DDIM loop is VOID_DDIM.

NAG scale is off by one between camps: core and the ComfyUI-NAG forks use z₊φ − z₋(φ−1), while sd-perturbed-attention, Anima-NAG and Krea2-NAG use z₊ + φ(z₊−z₋). The same number is not the same strength.
"NAG" in RT-RareTools never touches attention: it runs the formula on whole denoised predictions.
belgiangurista SMC-CFG has no sliding surface or state; lambda and warm-up inputs are unused, and it adds −k·sign(e).
S²-Guidance: ceil wraps only pct/100, so any non-zero percentage skips every block.
bvhari PerpNeg's variable "perp" is the parallel projection of positive on negative, the reverse geometry of core.
Negative-attention builds a new randomly initialised nn.Linear on each attention call, so its effect depends on RNG state.
sd-perturbed-attention FDG calls project and then adds both parts straight back, so the projection is a no-op.
Core CFGNorm's strength multiplies the whole x0 (0 gives x̂=0), and its pre_cfg=true mode installs a cfg function, not a pre-CFG hook.

RISK: eval/exec in shared workflows. A static scan found `eval(`/`exec(` in 103 of 865 section-28 packs (some false positives). Real text-widget cases: ``, `` (passes real `__builtins__` beside a "restricted scope" comment), `` (numpy namespace in eval globals). Core uses simpleeval instead, ``.

Frequency bands inverted: both mask an unshifted FFT with a centre-based radius, so "low" and "high" are swapped. `` and `TensorVizion__OmniNodes/Creative Intelligent Nodes`. Reasoned from code, not run.

Core lanczos is unsafe for latents: it clips to 0..1 and quantises to 8 bits, ``. LatentUpscale hides it from its combo, but any pack passing it to common_upscale hits it. FlowMatching-Upscaler guards at ``.
Core LatentInterpolate norm lacks keepdim, ``, so by broadcasting rules batch>1 errors, and batch==channels silently pairs the wrong axes. Reasoned from code, not run.
WAS BlendLatents rescales every output to 0..1, ``; soft_light takes sqrt of raw values at :75, giving NaN on negatives.
"bislerp" blend in PPFN/Apt_Preset is lerp plus min-max rescale, ``; bleh keeps the formula under the name bislerp_wrong at ``. Also PPFN adjust truncates to 4 channels, ``.

In-place writes and hijacks: MTB lerp overwrites the upstream tensor through `out=` after a shallow copy, ``; ReSharpen monkeypatches latent_preview at import and edits sampler x in a preview callback, ``.
PowerNoiseSuite "blue", "green" and "pink" are one filter with different default alpha: all divide the FFT by |f|^(α/2), so "blue" (α=2) has a 1/f² power spectrum, the reverse of real blue noise.
Sonar's named "white" is only ±1 (sign(n)·|n|⁰) and "velvet" reduces to Gaussian (sign(n)·|n| = n): the color names here mean pointwise remaps with a flat spectrum, not a spectrum shape.
SUNoise is not uniform noise at every step: even steps are plain Gaussian, and odd steps are uniform that skip both s_noise and σ_up.
City96's "LatentGaussianNoise" is uniform draws in hardcoded per-channel ranges (for example −22 to 33), far from unit variance.
Restart sampling in auto mode at 20+ steps discards your schedule and rebuilds sigmas as Karras.
Core s_churn on euler and heun uses torch.randn_like and ignores noise_sampler, so custom-noise nodes never reach it.
PPFN's Brownian hijack swaps the core class in module scope and mixes its fancy noise at a fixed 0.03 weight, so the "power noise" contribution per step is small by construction.
CADS adds its noise to prompt embeddings, not latents, then restores embedding mean and std; the latent is untouched.

ppm's Euler SMEA Dy gates its extra calls with `i + 1 // 2 == 1` and `== 0`. Python precedence makes these fire only on steps 1 and 0. . Same file's Euler Dy gate `i // 2 == 1` fires only at steps 2 and 3. Same file line 89.
Three of the TCD forks (licyk, dfl, SeedV) compute `sigma_to_s` from (1−γ)t and never use it, so gamma only toggles the DDPM variance on or off.

Euler extended sigmas' churn term is `(sigma_hat ** 2 - sigma_hat ** 2) ** 0.5`, always zero, and it divides by n_sub−1 which is zero for unsubdivided steps when s_churn>0. comfyui-lopi999-nodes sampler_list.py:223 (repo path in the entry).
MD AMED has no mean-value midpoint: it is Heun with a sigma-dependent derivative blend. . Boyo "Richardson" is a weighted x0 average, not extrapolation. See entry richardson-x0-accumulator for path.
MD PingPong imports `pingpong_sampler_core_bin` first and uses the source only as fallback, so a compiled binary would take priority if present.

Extra-Samplers-Plus ships two `sample_ttm_jvp` bodies differing only in φ₂ (h vs h_η).  vs other_samplers. The Clyb 4M docstring blames Bard and ChatGPT if its citation is wrong, extra_samplers.py:438.
Clyb BDF has no backward-difference table; it is a lerp predictor with elementwise atan and projection scaling.
SADA's docstring says Adams-Bashforth 23/12,−16/12,5/12 simplifies to 0.625,0.75,−0.375; the code uses the latter and they are not equal.
Core ToMe merges only the queries: `return m(q), k, v` leaves keys and values at full length, despite the name.
Core HyperTile tiles q but returns k and v in whole-image layout, so the backend views them into the larger batch in raster order (inference from attention.py:1096-1123).
Negative Attention builds a new untrained torch.nn.Linear on every attention call, so its correction term is random each call.
TurboTeaCache's Wan polynomial is all positive with constant 0.4945; default threshold is 0.15, so on Wan it should never skip at defaults (inference).

benjiyaya Spectrum truth-tests a sigma tensor with `or`; swallowed in spectrum_core.py:36, uncaught at nodes.py:130, while core always sets sample_sigmas, so a normal run should raise (inference, not run).
FreeU_Advanced and Sonar FreeU Extreme register `middle_block_patch`, a name nothing in this core reads, so their middle-block option does nothing.
Animemory replaces comfy.k_diffusion.sampling.sample_euler_ancestral at import, changing that sampler for every job if the pack is installed.
bleh's global Sage node overwrites __code__ on the live optimized_attention function, reaching code that imported it by name; KJNodes WanVideoTeaCacheKJ is now a no-op returning the model.

Same names, different curves. MD Hybrid's `ays`, `beta` and `simple` modes are a logistic blend, 1−(1−t^α)^β and smoothstep, and MD's GITS is a tanh warp with no tables; Adept's "AYS SDXL" table is near-uniform, not NVIDIA's.
Flux "shift" is the log of SD3 "shift": flux_time_shift with σ=1 equals time_snr_shift with α=e^μ, so the same number gives very different curves.  and :414
`denoise` means two things in core. BasicScheduler stretches and keeps `steps` steps; AYS, GITS and Optimal Steps cut to round(steps·denoise) steps.

Step counts that don't match the widget: ddim_uniform can return more than asked (read: N=1000, steps=30 gives 31 steps), beta can return fewer after removing repeats, and pack presets beta_32, beta_43 and beta_42 quietly add steps.
Core Laplace is the only core get_sigmas_* with no trailing zero, so it stops at sigma_min with residual noise.
Random inference schedules: the ai-toolkit-style `sigmoid` type draws unseeded torch.randn and sorts, so sigmas change each run.
A hard-coded Z-Image preset rises mid-run (.92 then .935), and core's ExtendIntermediateSigmas labels its sine curve 'cosine' and its cosine curve 'sine'.
Named schedulers that add nothing: TCDScheduler is core ddim_uniform and LCMScheduler is core sgm_uniform; "logSNR uniform" in Adept equals exponential when σmax>1.

Core's H3 PDD heads treat rows after the first as offsets from a full head, while CineConIA's loader says the official heads are full velocities and averages them all. The two may describe different file layouts (inference).
A hook-based LoRA is silently dropped on int8 H3 mlp.fc2, since core's fused call reads the weight and skips the module's forward. The live Turbo pack routes those layers to merge.

The NKD audio shift curve changes only the transformer option per step; ModelSamplingAV's audio_scale stays fixed, so the stream's effective schedule is not a plain re-shift (inference from reading both, not measured).

fxai-toolkit replaces comfy.model_base.MiniMaxH3 at import, so video noise scaling becomes σε + x for every H3 in the process. Core's MiniMaxH3SigmaShift builds a fresh sampling object, which would drop it (inference).
DaSiWa's H3 cache was filed under first-block-cache but runs no block to decide; it compares the stack's input, and it carries a full copy of core's H3 _forward to get a patch point.
CachedSearch uses a step cache only for ranking seeds, then re-renders the winner with the cache off, so the delivered latent is uncached.
ROCm's H3 EasyCache tooltip reads start_percent as a step fraction, but core converts the percent to a sigma, which does not map that way on a shift-12 schedule (reading core, not measured).
Kayarte's AudioNoiseMapper, with NOISE in its name, generates no noise: it returns a dict of parameters computed from audio energy.
LanPaint's Friction input still flows into Gamma, but only the commented-out damped scheme used Gamma, so the knob does nothing.
SUPREME adds its inner substep noise to z_k after z_avg was accumulated, and z_k is reset next substep, so it never reaches the output.
SUPREME substeps all restart from the same x, so with one method and no history term they average identical results.
Gigachad's CFG rescale divides x.std() by itself plus epsilon, so it is a no-op at any strength.
Radiance's apply_cfg_plus_plus is a cosine decay of the scale toward 1, unrelated to the CFG++ update.
RALU's Flux path calls forward_orig itself, so CFG, patches and ComfyUI samplers do not apply.
LatentTools' DownsampledLatentGuidance has its downscale lines commented out and now feeds a re-noised reference latent, at three extra cond calls.
TwinFlow ignores graph sigmas apart from their count, and with r=1 discards the noise estimate each step.
